Orbit geometry and field-line connection are saved to the Store by default (cache="use"), so later loads only read them back. Results loaded with missing="empty" or "warn" while source files were missing are not saved.

docs.title: Solar zenith angle
docs.text:
kg.orbit.sza computes the solar zenith angle at the sub-spacecraft point from the Sun direction given by SPICE. When no kernels are passed and the download policy is not never, NAIF generic kernels are fetched automatically (Coordinate Frames). To give the Sun direction yourself, use sun_vector=.

sza = kg.orbit.sza.load(time)
sza = kg.orbit.sza.load(time, sun_vector=[1.0, 0.0, 0.0], sun_frame="MOON_ME")

Orbit positions can be transformed to another frame while loading by passing frame= and context= (a FrameContext).

docs.title: Field-line connection to the surface
docs.text:
magnetic_connection extends a straight line from the spacecraft along the local field direction and checks whether it meets a sphere of radius radius_km (default 1737.4 km). Both the field direction (plus) and the opposite direction (minus) are checked (direction="both").

conn = kg.lmag.magnetic_connection.load(time)
conn.plot(kind="footpoint")      # footpoint, altitude, incidence, distance
conn.to_xarray()
Variable Meaning connected_any, connected_plus, connected_minus Whether either or each direction meets the sphere footpoint_plus_lon, footpoint_plus_lat, … Longitude and latitude of the intersection (deg) distance_plus_km, distance_minus_km Distance to the intersection incidence_angle_plus_deg, incidence_angle_minus_deg Acute angle between the field line and the surface normal altitude_km Spacecraft altitude

This is a straight-line geometry and does not include field-line bending by crustal magnetic anomalies. Tracing through a surface field model is available as an experimental API (sopran.experimental.moon.svm3d).

docs.title: Matching another instrument's times
docs.text:
To match the times of another instrument such as PACE, use resample_like.

esa1 = kg.esa1.counts.load(time, missing="warn")
conn_on_esa1 = conn.resample_like(esa1, method="nearest", tolerance="2s")
altitude_on_esa1 = altitude.resample_like(esa1, method="linear", tolerance="10s")

The methods are listed in Time Alignment.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• There are no tests comparing the SPICE Sun direction and frame transforms with SPEDAS geometry yet.
  • Altitude and sub-spacecraft points use a spherical Moon without terrain (DEM).

docs.title: LRS (Plasma Waves And Radio)
docs.text:
Of LRS (Lunar Radar Sounder), SOPRAN reads the public spectra (CDF) of the two receivers that measure natural radio and plasma waves.

Entry point Receiver Contents kg.lrs.npw NPW (Natural Plasma Wave) Spectra of receivers 1 and 2 kg.lrs.wfc WFC-H (Waveform Capture, high-frequency side) Electric-field spectra plus gain, mode, and other support data

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
Entry point Dimensions Units Meaning npw.rx1, npw.rx2 time, frequency dB NPW spectra npw.mode time flag NPW mode wfc.ex_db, wfc.ey_db time, frequency dB Raw WFC spectra wfc.ex_field, wfc.ey_field time, frequency dB uV/m Field level after gain and band correction wfc.ex_power_spectral_density, wfc.ey_power_spectral_density time, frequency (V/m)^2/Hz Electric-field power spectral density wfc.gain time dB Gain decoded from the Gain flag wfc.mode, wfc.xymode, wfc.fband, wfc.omode, wfc.postgap time flag Raw Mode byte, the modes decoded from it, and the PostGap flag wfc.pdc_ti, wfc.pdc_ti_words time (pdc_word) count Spacecraft time counter (not UTC)

Names directly under the instrument, such as kg.lrs.wfc_ey_power_spectral_density, reach the same endpoints.

kg = spn.kaguya
time = spn.period("2008-04-01T00:00:00", "2008-04-01T02:00:00")

npw = kg.lrs.npw.rx1.load(time, missing="warn")
psd = kg.lrs.wfc.ey_power_spectral_density.load(time)

spn.stack(
    npw.spectrogram(y="frequency", log_color=True),
    psd.spectrogram(y="frequency", log_color=True),
    kg.lrs.wfc.gain.load(time).line(),
).plot()

docs.title: Source files
docs.text:
NPW has one file per day and WFC one file per two hours. A range starting at an odd hour, such as 01:00–01:30, still reads the preceding 00:00 WFC file.

raw/kaguya/pds3/
  sln-l-lrs-5-npw-spectrum-v1.0/YYYYMMDD/data/LRS_NPW_V010_YYYYMMDD.cdf
  sln-l-lrs-4-wfc-spectrum-v1.0/YYYYMMDD/data/LRS_WFC_V010_YYYYMMDDhhmmss.cdf

docs.title: Caching
docs.text: LRS endpoints save what they read to the Store with cache="use" (default). Raw NPW and WFC spectra go to the normalized layer; gain, field level, power spectral density, and modes go to features. Reading the same period again does not reread the CDF. Results loaded with missing="empty" or "warn" while source files were missing are not saved.

docs.title: Corrections and missing values
docs.text:
• Field level and power spectral density follow the dB correction and bandwidth normalization of SPEDAS (kgy_lrs_load.pro) and lunarsat.
  • Values filled by the CDF sparse-record padding are kept distinct from observed zeros. For WFC support variables UINT1 254, and for PDC-TI [65534, 0, 65534], are treated as missing. These differ from the CDF FILLVAL=0.
  • Times come from the CDF Epoch (UTC). wfc_pdc_ti is a 48-bit on-board counter built from high, middle, and low 16-bit words; it is not converted to UTC without a conversion table. The raw three words stay in wfc_pdc_ti_words.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only WFC-H spectra can be read. WFC-L waveforms (10 Hz–100 kHz) are a separate product from the public spectra and are not supported.
  • There is no long-term comparison test with SPEDAS on real data yet.

Wave-event candidate extraction is in Experimental.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
• Y. Kasahara et al., "Plasma wave observation using waveform capture in the Lunar Radar Sounder on board the SELENE spacecraft," Earth, Planets and Space 60, 341–351 (2008). doi:10.1186/BF03352799
  • DARTS KAGUYA archive

docs.title: PACE (Electrons And Ions)
docs.text:
PACE (Plasma energy Angle and Composition Experiment) is the set of four particle analyzers on KAGUYA. SOPRAN reads the public PBF1 (v3.0) files and uses the same variable names for all four.

Entry point Sensor Particles kg.esa1 ESA-S1 Electrons kg.esa2 ESA-S2 Electrons kg.ima IMA Ions (mass analysis) kg.iea IEA Ions

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
Variable Dimensions Units Meaning counts time, energy, look count Raw counts energy_flux time, energy, look eV/(cm^2 s sr eV) Differential energy flux computed from counts with the calibration tables energy energy channel / eV Energy channel index when uncalibrated, energy center in eV when calibrated quality time flag Record quality flag

look is the index of a detector viewing direction, not the direction itself. Directions (polar and azimuth angles) require the calibration tables; the pitch-angle spectra below use them. energy_flux has the aliases eflux and differential_energy_flux.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
kg = spn.kaguya
time = spn.day("2008-01-01")

flux = kg.esa1.energy_flux.load(time)       # SopranArray
esa1 = kg.esa1.load(time)                   # instrument-level result

esa1.counts, esa1.energy_flux, esa1.quality
esa1.to_xarray()                            # xarray.Dataset with all variables
esa1.to_polars("counts", reduce_look="sum") # table summed over look
esa1.files                                  # source files
esa1.pace                                   # decoded headers and records

To decode source files directly, use sopran.missions.kaguya.read_pace_pbf(files). Decoding runs in the Rust extension and falls back to the Python reference implementation when the extension is missing (backend="auto").

docs.title: Energy flux calibration
docs.text:
energy_flux is computed from counts as

\[ \mathrm{energy\_flux} = \frac{\mathrm{counts}}{t_\mathrm{integ}\; G\; \varepsilon} \]

where \(t_\mathrm{integ}\) is the integration time, \(G\) the g-factor from the PACE INFO table, and \(\varepsilon\) the detection efficiency. The default \(\varepsilon = 0.6\) is the uniform value used by SPEDAS kgy_esa1_get3d.pro and kgy_esa2_get3d.pro. For another value, call kg.esa1.load(time).to_energy_flux(efficiency=...).

The calibration tables (INFO and FOV) load automatically. They come from the same distribution as SPEDAS kgy_read_inf.pro and kgy_read_fov.pro, which is served over HTTP only. Retrieved tables are recorded in the Store's source-file registry with their URL and sha256. Without the tables, loading energy_flux raises; uncalibrated values are never returned under that name. After calibration the energy coordinate holds energy centers in eV, and the original channel index stays in the energy_channel coordinate.

cal = kg.esa1.load_calibration(download="never")   # read the tables explicitly
esa1 = kg.esa1.load(time, calibration=cal)

All four sensors use the same formula and table handling. Regression tests cover ESA1; the flux of ESA2, IMA, and IEA has not been compared numerically with SPEDAS yet.

docs.title: Missing value 65535
docs.text: PBF1 counts are 16-bit unsigned integers. Following the SPEDAS PACE readers (kgy_read_pbf.pro, kgy_esa1_get3d.pro), SOPRAN converts the maximum value 65535 to NaN as missing. The PDS3 labels we checked declare no missing value such as MISSING_CONSTANT. Zero counts stay zero.

docs.title: Pitch-angle spectra
docs.text:
pitch_angle_spectrum() turns look back into directions with the calibration tables and bins by the angle to the magnetic field, producing a time × energy × pitch_angle array.

from sopran.missions.kaguya import selene_spice_kernels

b = kg.lmag.magnetic_field.load(time)                         # MOON_ME
frames = spn.FrameContext(spice_kernels=selene_spice_kernels(kg.store, time))   # fetch Moon and attitude kernels

pas = kg.esa1.energy_flux.pitch_angle_spectrum(
    time,
    magnetic_field=b,
    frame_context=frames,             # rotate the MOON_ME field into the PACE viewing frame
    pitch_bins="native",
    cache="use",
)
pas.plot()                                          # pitch vs time and energy vs time
pas.energy_spectrogram(pitch=(0.0, 30.0), log_color=True)

A fixed vector in the viewing frame, such as magnetic_field=[1.0, 0.0, 0.0], works without kernels for quick tests.

Argument Meaning magnetic_field Required. A vector in the viewing frame, or a SopranArray that carries its frame look_frame, magnetic_frame Frames of the viewing directions (default SELENE_M_SPACECRAFT) and the field. When they differ, pass a FrameContext as frame_context pitch_bins "native" (16 bins for 4×16-direction records, 32 for 16×64; the larger on mixed days), a bin count, or bin edges min_look_bins Minimum number of viewing directions per pitch-angle bin count_correction "none" (default), "event", "trash", "event_trash"; corresponds to SPEDAS /cntcorr cache With "use", results with the same arguments are saved in the features layer and reused

count_correction="trash" redistributes discarded counts (trash counters) over azimuth, and "event" scales adjacent energy pairs to the event counter. The correction is kept as a separate multiplier, so raw counts remain integers.

Results carry the per-record exposure and the coordinates pace_data_mode, pace_data_type, pace_submode, pace_svs_tbl, pace_data_quality, and record_duration_seconds. Whether a record may be used for pitch angles is decided from the observation mode; the rules are in PACE ESA Mode Policy.

docs.title: Ion 3-D distributions (IMA and IEA)
docs.text:
ion_distribution() turns IMA and IEA records into 3-D distributions shaped like those of SPEDAS kgy_ima_get3d and kgy_iea_get3d, returning one PaceIon3D per record type.

time = spn.day("2009-02-17")
iea = kg.iea.load(time, calibration=kg.iea.load_calibration()).ion_distribution(
    count_correction="event_trash"
)
d = iea[0x81]                       # 32 energy × 16 polar × 64 azimuth
d.counts                            # (record, 32, bin), bin = polar + azimuth × 16
d.to_units("eflux")                 # counts / rate / eflux / flux / df
d.density()                         # cm^-3
d.velocity()                        # km/s, SELENE_M_SPACECRAFT

from sopran.frames import FrameContext
from sopran.missions.kaguya import selene_spice_kernels

context = FrameContext(spice_kernels=tuple(map(str, selene_spice_kernels(kg.store, time))))
d.velocity(frame="MOON_ME", context=context)
d.directions(frame="MOON_ME", context=context)   # direction of motion for each bin
Type Sensor Shape Handling 0x40 IMA 4 polar × 32 energy × 1024 TOF TOF summed; no azimuth (dphi = 360°); gfactor of azimuth channel 4 0x41 IMA 32 × 16 × 64 0x42 IMA 32 × 4 × 16 0x43 IMA 8 mass × 32 × 4 × 16 mass channels summed 0x80 IEA 32 × 4 × 16 0x81 IEA 32 × 16 × 64

Other types (IMA 0x44 and 0x45, IEA 0x82) are not handled by SPEDAS either; the skipped counts are listed in notes.

  • Energies, angles and geometric factors come from the INFO tables, placed by the energy and polar sequence numbers (angles="fov" uses the FOV tables). grids holds one grid per RAM table and grid_index maps records to it.
  • theta_deg and phi_deg give the direction of particle motion. In the solar wind on 2009-02-17, 99.7% of the IEA speed pointed anti-sunward after conversion to MOON_ME.
  • IMA mass channels are summed and treated as protons, as in SPEDAS.
  • Units follow kgy_pace_convert_units and moments kgy_n_3d and kgy_j_3d, with efficiency 0.6 (the SPEDAS placeholder). No dead-time correction is applied.
  • Count correction is the SPEDAS /cntcorr. IMA uses the sum of the three TOF event rows, and type 0x40 has no trash telemetry, so only the event step is applied.
  • Differences from SPEDAS: cells whose mass channels are all fill values stay NaN (SPEDAS gives 0), and the energy widths denergy_eV are absolute values.

Checked on 2009-02-17 (solar wind): IEA speed was 0.99–1.00 times OMNI and density 0.46–0.70 times. On the dayside (SZA < 45°) the IMA flux moving away from the Moon was about 0.7–0.9% of the solar-wind flux (OMNI nv).

docs.title: Saving to Parquet
docs.text:
record = (
    kg.esa1.energy_flux.pipeline(spn.period("2008-01-01", "2008-01-03"))
    .calibrate(calibration="auto")
    .write("kaguya.esa1.energy_flux", layer="normalized", partition="day")
    .run()
)

To save counts, start from kg.esa1.counts.pipeline(...) and drop calibrate. Running pipelines is covered in Batch Pipelines.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Saved Parquet does not yet include look directions (polar and azimuth angles) or energy coordinate metadata.
  • ESA2, IMA, and IEA energy flux has not been compared numerically with SPEDAS.
  • ion_distribution() densities use efficiency 0.6; IEA solar-wind density is 30–50% below OMNI. IMA TOF mass separation (kgy_read_tof) is not implemented yet.
  • The bit meanings of data_quality are not settled in public documents, so the value is kept as is in pace_data_quality.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
• PACE format description (JAXA DARTS)
  • SPEDAS kgy_read_pbf.pro, kgy_esa1_get3d.pro, kgy_ima_get3d.pro, kgy_iea_get3d.pro, kgy_pace_convert_units.pro
  • Saito, Y., et al. (2008), Solar wind proton reflection at the lunar surface: Low energy ion measurement by MAP-PACE onboard SELENE (KAGUYA), GRL.

docs.title: Moon Maps
docs.text:
Maps fixed to the lunar surface, such as terrain (DEM), surface magnetic field (SVM), solar zenith angle, illumination, and shadow, are handled through the body spn.moon rather than a mission. Whichever mission a map comes from, it means the same thing in use: a quantity on lunar longitude and latitude. GeoTIFF maps are read with rasterio (moon extra).

moon = spn.moon
region = spn.Region(lon=(120, 160), lat=(-45, -10), body="moon")

dem = moon.dem.load(source="lro.lola.dem_118m", region=region)
sza = moon.sza.compute(like=dem, subsolar_lon_lat=(0.0, 0.0))
shadow = moon.shadow.compute(method="terrain_ray", dem=dem, sza=sza)

docs.title: Map types
docs.text:
Entry point Aliases Units Meaning moon.dem elevation, height m Elevation moon.svm surface_vector_map, svm_tsunakawa2015 nT Tsunakawa et al. (2015) surface magnetic field map; the default SVM moon.svm_ravat2020 — nT Ravat et al. (2020) surface field model with a selectable component moon.sza solar_zenith_angle deg Solar zenith angle moon.illumination illumination_map fraction Illumination moon.shadow shadow_map fraction Shadow

Maps can also be selected by name, as in moon.map("elevation"). Loaded maps are RasterLayer objects, and dem.sample(lat=0.5, lon=10.5) returns values at arbitrary points. Each map's info(), guide(), example(), and sources() describe it and its available sources.

docs.title: Coordinate conventions
docs.text:
Longitude and latitude definitions are never implicit; they are kept in the plan (plan()) and in result metadata.

Key Example values Default lon_domain 0_360, -180_180 0_360 lon_direction east_positive, west_positive east_positive lat_type planetocentric, planetographic planetocentric shape spherical, spice_body_radii spherical projection native, polar_stereographic native area_or_point area, point area

Regions crossing 0/360 can be written as spn.Region(lon=(350, 10), ...) (Time, Regions, And Cases).

plan = moon.dem.plan(source="lro.lola.dem_118m", region=region, projection="polar_stereo")
plan.to_metadata()      # check conventions and inputs before reading

docs.title: DEM
docs.text:
source Contents Size lro.lola.dem_118m (lro.lola.dem) LRO LOLA global DEM, 256 pixels/deg (118 m at the equator) About 8 GB lro.lola.sldem2015_59m (kaguya.tc.dem) SLDEM2015, merged LOLA and KAGUYA Terrain Camera, 512 pixels/deg, 60°S–60°N About 22 GB

Both download directly from USGS into the Store's raw/moon/dem/.

path = moon.dem.download(source="lro.lola.dem_118m")      # into the default Store
dem = moon.dem.load(path=path, source="lro.lola.dem_118m", region=region)

Without path=, load() reads the file in the Store's raw/moon/dem/. When it is missing, the same download policy as other data applies (Configuration, default missing), so the file is retrieved first. DEMs are 8–22 GB; to avoid retrieval, pass download="never" or set the session or View policy to never. Missing files then raise DatasetNotFoundError. Choose the Store with store=; otherwise spn.moon uses the session settings and view.moon the Store of its Project.

With region=, only the part of the file covering the region is read. Regions crossing 0/360 cannot be split into windows yet, so the whole file is read.

docs.title: Surface magnetic field (SVM)
docs.text:
The Tsunakawa SVM (LunarSVM_000_02_v02.dat, ver. 2) gives the three surface components of the lunar magnetic anomalies derived from low-altitude Kaguya and Lunar Prospector magnetometer data (Tsunakawa et al. 2015; ver. 2 in Tsunakawa et al. 2023). moon.svm.download() fetches the file that the LMAG team distributes on Google Drive as a supplement of the 2023 paper and places it in the Store's raw/moon/svm/ only when it matches the registered SHA-256. With the default download policy (missing), load() fetches it when the file is absent.

path = moon.svm.download()                      # about 165 MB, into the Store
svm = moon.svm.load()                           # read from the Store, fetching it if absent
svm = moon.svm.load(path="/path/to/LunarSVM_000_02_v02.dat")
svm.sample(lat=-0.5, lon=0.0)

The distributor's folder (globalSVM_v02_2022) also holds the files below. SOPRAN does not fetch them automatically; download them in a browser when you need them.

File Contents LunarSVM_SHC_v02.dat Spherical harmonic coefficients \(g_n^m, h_n^m\) (\(n\le450\), \(R=1737.4\) km). About 4 MB; regenerates the grid and the field at any altitude Bcal_v02.f90 The official Fortran program that computes the field above the surface from the surface Br Positions.dat, B_Positions_v02.rst Example input and output of Bcal_v02.f90, used to validate SVM3D Readme_v02.txt Outline of the ver. 2 data selection and processing

Ver. 1 (2015) is in globalSVM_v01_2015 of the same supplement, together with the lists of observation periods used (Periods_KGused.dat, Periods_LPused.dat). The original location http://www.geo.titech.ac.jp/lab/tsunakawa/Kaguya_LMAG was unreachable as of October 2026.

The distributor states no license. SOPRAN neither bundles nor redistributes the files; it only links to the distributor and provides the download procedure. Cite Tsunakawa et al. (2015, 2023) when you use the map.

The Ravat et al. (2020) model (moon.svm_ravat2020) is a surface field derived from along-track magnetic field gradients of Lunar Prospector and KAGUYA. It is given on a 0.1-degree grid on the lunar ellipsoid (equatorial radius 1738.1 km, polar radius 1736.0 km), and component= selects the component.

component Meaning "total" (default) Total field "br" Radial component (positive outward) "btheta" Colatitudinal component (positive southward) "bphi" Azimuthal component (positive eastward)

The University of Kentucky repository that distributes it (DOI 10.13023/9wpe-tt68, CC0) stops scripted downloads with a browser check, so SOPRAN cannot retrieve it. Download the main file Ravatetal_JGR2020_LunarL1MagneticModelFields_LPgrad.dat (about 88 MB) in a web browser and place it in the Store's raw/moon/svm/ or pass it as path=. Loading builds the grid from about 6.5 million rows and takes a few seconds.

br = moon.svm_ravat2020.load(component="br")    # read from the Store's raw/moon/svm/
br.sample(lat=8.0, lon=302.0)                   # near Reiner Gamma

docs.title: Solar zenith angle, illumination, and shadow
docs.text:
moon.sza.compute() computes the solar zenith angle on a spherical Moon. Give the grid as an existing map (like=) or with lon=, lat=, region=. Give the Sun position with one of:

Argument Sun position sun_vector= Sun direction vector in Moon-fixed coordinates subsolar_lon_lat= Longitude and latitude of the subsolar point time= and spice_kernels= Computed with SPICE (needs leap-second, lunar frame, and ephemeris kernels) 
sza = moon.sza.compute(like=dem, subsolar_lon_lat=(0.0, 0.0))
illumination = moon.illumination.compute(sza=sza, threshold_deg=90.0)   # 1 where sza <= 90
shadow = moon.shadow.compute(sza=sza, threshold_deg=90.0)               # 1 where sza > 90

Threshold illumination and shadow are binary maps without terrain. Shadows cast by topography use method="terrain_ray", which follows the horizon over the DEM toward the Sun.

sza = moon.sza.compute(
    like=dem,
    time="2008-02-01T12:00:00Z",
    spice_kernels=("kernels/naif0012.tls", "kernels/de421.bsp", "kernels/moon_pa.bpc"),
)
shadow = moon.shadow.compute(method="terrain_ray", dem=dem, sza=sza)

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Reprojection and bilinear interpolation are not implemented; projection is used for records and plans.
  • The Sun is treated as a point source, so partial shadow (penumbra) is not computed.
  • terrain_ray is slow on large DEMs, and numerical validation with public DEMs and real SPICE kernels has not been done.

To search anomaly locations from published tables, use the Magnetic Anomaly Catalog.

docs.title: Magnetic Anomaly Catalog
docs.text:
spn.moon.magnetic_anomalies() returns a list of lunar magnetic anomalies built from published location tables, as a pandas.DataFrame. The tables are bundled with the package, so no network access or SVM file is needed.

import sopran as spn

sites = spn.moon.magnetic_anomalies()       # corrected Blewett (2011) table, 15 entries
sites[["name", "lon_deg", "lat_deg", "peak_field_30km_nt", "swirl"]]

# substring match on name and feature_id; handles Gamma/γ, hyphens, and underscores
reiner = spn.moon.magnetic_anomalies("all", name="Reiner Gamma")

# search near (east longitude, latitude); 57.5°W can be -57.5 or 302.5
nearby = spn.moon.magnetic_anomalies("all", near=(-57.5, 7.5), radius_deg=5)

# analysis centers of isolated anomalies and the observation radii used in the paper
isolated = spn.moon.magnetic_anomalies("oliveira2017")

docs.title: Included tables
docs.text:
catalog Contents Source blewett2011 (default) 15 entries: approximate location, peak field at 30 km altitude, terrain setting, swirl classification at the time Blewett et al. (2011), corrected Table 1 oliveira2017 15 entries: analysis centers of isolated anomalies, observation radius \(r_o\), dipole placement radius \(r_d\) Oliveira & Wieczorek (2017), Table 1 all 30 rows from both tables, 23 feature_id values; different published values for the same region stay in separate rows Both tables

This is the list of regions chosen in the literature, not a complete inventory of lunar magnetic anomalies. name keeps the published spelling, and feature_id links Reiner-γ with Reiner Gamma and Sirsalis with Rima Sirsalis. Rows with different coordinates are never averaged or merged. Blewett's original paper has coordinate errors, so the corrected table is used.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Column Meaning lon_deg, lat_deg Published Moon-fixed coordinates, east longitude 0–360°, north latitude positive. No precise MOON_ME/MOON_PA conversion is applied position_kind approximate_anomaly_location for approximate locations, analysis_center for the center of an analysis region peak_field_30km_nt Estimated regional peak \(\lvert B\rvert\) at 30 km altitude (nT); not a surface value or a point value at the listed coordinates setting, swirl Terrain and swirl classification from Blewett's table; not_recognized means not recognized as of 2011 observation_radius_deg, dipole_radius_deg Angular radii of the analysis regions in Oliveira's paper; not physical boundaries or sizes of the anomalies reference_doi, note Per-row source and notes; Marginis has sparse Lunar Prospector magnetometer coverage distance_deg, distance_km Only with near: great-circle distance to the listed coordinates; km uses a lunar radius of 1737.4 km

Values absent from the literature are missing. With near, rows are sorted by distance, and radius_deg keeps rows whose listed point is within that angular distance. It cannot test intersections with regions. Give radius_deg together with near, between 0 and 180°. Empty results keep their columns and the DataFrame.attrs metadata.

docs.title: Combining with the SVM
docs.text:
To combine the location table with the SVM, pass the coordinates to the SVM's sample(). The added column is the SVM point value, a different quantity from the published regional peak.

svm = spn.moon.svm.load(path="/path/to/LunarSVM_000_02_v02.dat")
sites["svm_surface_point_nt"] = svm.sample(lat=sites.lat_deg, lon=sites.lon_deg)

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text: These are the criteria for deciding SOPRAN's public API and internal implementation. Check new features and data sources against them. The rules here are the ones the current implementation follows; decided plans and unimplemented ideas are kept in the last two sections.

docs.title: Intended experience
docs.text:
1. Users learn the structure and meaning of the data while using it, even without prior expertise. spn.kaguya.esa1.energy_flux reads as mission, instrument, and quantity, and types, completion, info(), units, frames, and time, energy, and viewing bins follow the same structure. File formats, distribution servers, and Rust implementation details never leak into quantity names.
  2. One path leads from the standard entry point to a figure. A short call such as plot(time) goes through retrieval, calibration, storage, and reloading to a figure whose axes and colorbar show quantities and units. Automation never hides the applied corrections, input files, settings, or processing history, and missing data or model misfits are never replaced with other values.
  3. Source files and native bins stay reachable. Results are not locked into processed values: source files (files) and records before calibration, rebinning, or time integration (such as PACE pace) remain in the loaded result.

docs.title: API contract
docs.text:
• Getting attributes is discovery only. Mission, instrument, variable, and Moon map attributes return lightweight objects and never download, decode, scan, or compute.
  • Work starts at a few well-defined points. load() reads data, compute() derives products from inputs, and plot() draws figures. For pipelines these are run(), collect(), scan(), and stream(). An endpoint's plot(time) is a convenience that loads data; outputs meant to keep their conditions use quicklook().
  • Every level offers the same discovery tools: info() (short description), guide() (detailed description), schema() (machine-readable definition), plan() (plan before running), and example() (runnable example).
  • Meaningful names are canonical. Names such as energy_flux and magnetic_field are the primary form in docs, plot labels, and schemas; short names such as eflux and b are aliases listed by info(). Aliases not in the specification are not added.
  • Results carry types, units, frames, times, and bins. Type boundaries with external libraries are explicit, and Any is not chained.
  • Configuration resolves in one place. Process defaults use spn.config.use(), temporary changes spn.config.using(), and everything else resolves through existing settings, Projects, and Views. Only resolve_store_roots() decides the Store root and only resolve_download_mode() the download policy, so every entry point gets the same result. Creating a Store never changes global settings, and no per-instrument global state is introduced.
  • Data sources are added by registration. Missions and bodies register themselves with register_source() in their own packages, and core never imports missions (Adding A Data Source).

docs.title: Schemas live in code
docs.text: Variable names, dimensions, units, data types, frames, and aliases are written in code as InstrumentSchema and VariableSchema. info(), validation (validate_schema), the Store's schema.json, plot axis labels and default logarithmic scales (log_scale, log_dims), and the Schemas page all come from them, which keeps hand-written tables and per-name special cases from drifting.

docs.title: Storage and reproducibility
docs.text:
• Processed data is saved and reloaded through the existing product and cache mechanisms. Cache keys come from settings and input content, so results under different settings are never reused as the same entry.
  • File lookup goes through the Store, layouts, and providers; machine-specific absolute paths are never embedded in the package.
  • The Store stays copyable with rsync. Manifests and catalogs contain only root-relative paths, and shard sidecars are the source of truth (Moving A Store).
  • Missing values, zeros, not-retrieved data, calibration state, and quality flags are kept distinct.
  • Schemas of saved datasets change even more carefully than the public API; incompatible changes bump the schema version.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: import sopran needs only numpy and pandas. Mission, map, and plotting dependencies are split into extras by use and imported lazily on the path that needs them. Each extra lists only packages SOPRAN actually imports, and tests/test_project_metadata.py checks that match. pyproject.toml is the source of truth for dependencies and build settings.

docs.title: Reuse existing libraries
docs.text:
Time-scale conversion, ephemerides and attitude, standard coordinate transforms, generic CDF and PDS reading, and unit conversion are not reimplemented.

Area Library Body and spacecraft geometry, coordinate transforms spiceypy Geospace frames (GSE, GSM, SM) spacepy (planned) CDF cdflib Maps and DEMs rasterio Tables and Parquet polars, pyarrow Multidimensional arrays xarray Figures matplotlib, panel

Own implementations are allowed for mission-specific binary decoding, fixes for broken provider metadata, instrument calibrations missing from existing libraries, and ports to Rust for performance. Even then, add tests against an external library or the official specification. When matching SPEDAS behavior, record the source, units, and correction conditions (License And Porting).

docs.title: Rust extension boundary
docs.text:
Heavy deterministic processing (PACE decoding, pitch-angle binning, ER fits, field-line tracing) is delegated to the bundled Rust extension sopran._native.

  • Data crosses between Python and Rust in coarse units (file groups, arrays, problems, batches), not per record or per bin.
  • Results come back as regular Python types, and everyday APIs never expose the FFI.
  • The backend name and settings are recorded for reproducibility and debugging.
  • Before porting, small golden outputs are compared with a Python reference implementation or the official specification, and nothing silently falls back to Python.

docs.title: Isolating experiments
docs.text: Unsettled models and analysis steps live in sopran.experimental, and the regular API never depends on them. Experiments still get types, units, and tests, and their Store keys stay separate from regular products. No compatibility aliases or shims are added for unpublished APIs. Individual research runs, comparison figures, and interpretations go to working/, not the public documentation (Experimental).

docs.title: Package layout
docs.text: Location Role src/sopran/core/ Store, configuration, Project/Case/View, data types, Pipeline, plotting, time alignment src/sopran/missions/ KAGUYA, ARTEMIS, Lunar Prospector, and OMNI readers, instruments, and product APIs src/sopran/bodies/moon/ Moon products such as DEM, shadow, and SVM src/sopran/frames/, src/sopran/maps/ Coordinate and time conversion, shared map types src/sopran/experimental/ Experiments imported explicitly crates/sopran-native/ Rust extension sopran._native tests/ Regression tests built mostly on synthetic data and fixtures scripts/hpc/ Supercomputer environment setup and job templates docs/ Public documentation (Writing Documentation)

docs.title: Exceptions and error messages
docs.text:
All exceptions derive from SopranError and also from a standard exception.

Exception Also derives from When ConfigError ValueError Invalid configuration value DatasetNotFoundError LookupError Dataset or source file not found DownloadError OSError Retrieval failed DecodeError ValueError File could not be decoded SchemaError ValueError Dimensions, data type, units, or frame do not match the schema FrameTransformError ValueError Missing inputs for a coordinate transform, or unsupported transform PipelineError RuntimeError No pipeline backend, or unsupported operation BackendError RuntimeError Backend unavailable

Error messages include, where possible, the failing endpoint or dataset ID, the available candidates, the next call to try (info() or plan()), and which stage failed: retrieval, decoding, schema, or coordinate transform.

docs.title: Planned work
docs.text:
The following items are decided. Each gets its design, following these principles, when work starts.

Item Contents Main work Chandrayaan-1 SARA (SWIM, CENA) PDS3 at ESA PSA. 2008–2009 overlaps KAGUYA, allowing simultaneous comparisons Only raw counts (EDR) are published, so calibration has to be prepared Wind SWE and MFI CDF files at CDAWeb; the upstream solar-wind observations behind OMNI Reuse the ARTEMIS retrieval (newest version from the SPDF listing) LRO Diviner GCP Surface (bolometric) brightness temperature by local time from PDS, for surface charging and exosphere studies Return it as a Moon map on a grid with local time Lunar Prospector ER extensions Pitch angles and the high-rate ER (ER_HI_TS) Add pitch angles after checking the look-direction sign conventions in the literature ARTEMIS extensions Quality flags and selenocentric position Read *_data_quality for the quality flags

docs.title: Ideas
docs.text:
The following are ideas, not promised.

  • Interactive plotting (HoloViews, hvPlot, Datashader) and long-period quicklooks.
  • spacepy and astropy coordinate transform backends.
  • Moon map reprojection, shadows with penumbra, and faster terrain_ray.
  • A mission-independent generic pipeline backend and Rust processing stages.
  • Saving PACE viewing-direction and energy coordinate metadata.

docs.title: Writing Documentation
docs.text: How the public documentation is organized and the rules for writing it. When adding or changing a page, decide where it belongs here first.

docs.title: Readers and structure
docs.text:
The documentation serves three kinds of readers.

Reader Needs Mainly reads Analysts (primary readers) How to load data and make figures; what the data means and its caveats Getting Started, User Guide, Data Researchers using experiments Definitions of research models; how to run full-period computations Experimental Contributors Design criteria, extension steps, checks, and releases Development

Each section has a defined scope.

Section Contains Does not contain Getting Started Four pages read in order by newcomers, showing the minimal steps of one workflow Exhaustive options (link to the User Guide) User Guide How each feature works and how to use it, one topic per page Instrument-specific details (go to Data) Data Variables, units, frames, sources, calibration, quality, and limitations per data source Instrument-independent features (go to the User Guide) Experimental Usage, model definitions, and limits of experiments Results of specific runs, comparison figures, interpretations (go to working/) Reference Tables to look up: API, schemas, file formats, CLI, terms Procedures or history Development Design criteria and procedures for extending, checking, and releasing User-facing usage

docs.title: One topic, one page
docs.text:
When the same explanation appears on several pages, one gets updated and the others drift. Decide one page that owns each topic, and link to it from elsewhere. For example, Store layers are described only in Storing Data, and configuration precedence only in Configuration. Getting Started repeats a little to show the flow, but leaves details to the User Guide.

Implementation status follows the same rule and sits next to the feature: support per data source is in the table of the data overview, unimplemented points in each page's "Limitations" section, and plans and ideas in Design Principles. There is no separate "status" page.

docs.title: Page templates
docs.text:
Data pages follow this order so readers find the same information in the same place across instruments:

  1. What was measured and which data it is (one or two sentences), with the shortest code example
  2. Variables (entry point, dimensions, units, frame, meaning)
  3. Loading and plotting examples
  4. Retrieving and placing source files
  5. Calibration, missing values, and quality
  6. Limitations (unimplemented or unverified points)
  7. Sources

User Guide pages state the question they answer in the first one or two sentences, then alternate explanation and procedure. Argument lists go in tables.

docs.title: Style
docs.text:
• The Japanese pages use the polite form (です・ます) and lead with the conclusion. Headings are short sentences or noun phrases that tell what follows.
  • Terms follow the Glossary. API names, external specification names, and file names stay in their original form in code; in Japanese text, no space is inserted around them.
  • Math uses $...$ and $$...$$; units use the same notation as the schemas, such as nT and eV/(cm^2 s sr eV).
  • Do not repeat generic caveats; state limitations and unverified points that affect decisions, concretely and next to the explanation they concern.
  • Only include code examples checked against the implementation. Define illustrative variables such as time once per page.
  • Embed figures with Markdown, made from real data and stored under docs/assets/.

docs.title: Japanese and English
docs.text:
The Japanese pages (docs/ja/) are primary, and the English pages (docs/en/) mirror them at the same paths. The build uses mkdocs-static-i18n, writing Japanese at the site root and English under /en/. Navigation titles are written in Japanese in the nav of mkdocs.yml, and their English titles in nav_translations. A missing English page falls back to the Japanese one, but tests/test_docs_build.py checks that every page has an English version.

The Lang: 日本語/English switch at the top right is docs/overrides/partials/alternate.html, which moves to the page at the same path in the other language.

docs.title: Generated pages
docs.text: Page Generated from Update Schemas InstrumentSchema in code python -m sopran.schema_docs docs/ja/reference/schemas.md (English with --language en) Python API Docstrings (mkdocstrings) Automatic at build time; the page lists the classes and functions to include

docs.title: URLs referenced from code
docs.text:
Descriptions returned by guide() contain public documentation URLs. sopran.core.pages.public_doc_urls("data/kaguya/") builds both the Japanese and English URLs from a page path. When moving pages, update these constants and tests such as tests/test_docs_build.py.

Constant Location _PUBLIC_DOC_PATHS src/sopran/missions/kaguya/mission.py _PUBLIC_DOC_URLS src/sopran/missions/artemis/mission.py PUBLIC_DOC_URLS src/sopran/bodies/moon/guides.py

docs.title: Adding a page
docs.text:
1. Decide where it belongs using the tables above, and check that no page already covers the topic.
  2. Create the page at the same path under docs/ja/ and docs/en/.
  3. Add the Japanese title to nav in mkdocs.yml and the English title to nav_translations.
  4. Link to it from related pages.
  5. Confirm with python -m mkdocs build --strict that there are no broken links or anchors. mkdocs serve previews the site (requires pip install -e ".[docs]").

docs.title: Adding A Data Source
docs.text: How to make a new mission's or body's data available through spn.<name>, view.<name>, and spn.load("<name>..."). The smallest implementation is src/sopran/missions/omni/ (OMNI); reading it alongside this page helps.

docs.title: 1. Register
docs.text:
Each data source registers itself in its package's __init__.py. Because core never imports missions, registration happens on the mission side.

# src/sopran/missions/<name>/__init__.py
from sopran.core.sources import register_source

register_source("<name>", "sopran.missions.<name>.mission:<Mission>.from_view")

The second argument is "module:attribute.path" and is imported on first use. The registered factory receives a View and returns an object bound to that view's time range, download policy, and Store.

class Mission:
    def __init__(self, *, store: Store | None = None, download: DownloadMode | None = None,
                 view: View | None = None) -> None:
        self.store = store or Store()
        self.download = resolve_download_mode(download)   # leave policy resolution to one place
        self.view = view

    @classmethod
    def from_view(cls, view: View) -> "Mission":
        return cls(store=view.project.store, download=view.context.download, view=view)

Once src/sopran/__init__.py imports the package, registration is complete, and spn.<name>, view.<name>, case.<name>, and spn.load("<name>.…") all use the same object.

docs.title: 2. Write schemas
docs.text:
Write a VariableSchema per variable and group them in an InstrumentSchema per instrument. Units, dimensions, and frames are defined here.

DENSITY = VariableSchema(name="density", dims=("time",), units="cm^-3", description="Proton density.")
SCHEMA = InstrumentSchema(mission="<name>", instrument="<instrument>", variables=(DENSITY,))

Mark quantities spanning many decades (fluxes, power spectral densities) with log_scale=True, and coordinates drawn on a log axis with log_dims=("energy",). Array and endpoint plots take their default logarithmic scales from these hints.

To list the schema in the reference, add it to sopran.schema_docs.builtin_schemas() and regenerate the page with python -m sopran.schema_docs.

docs.title: 3. Build endpoints
docs.text:
Endpoints must not read files when they are merely retrieved as attributes. Provide at least:

Method Returns load(time=None, *, download=None, ...) SopranArray. Use view.time when time is omitted; if neither exists, raise with an example plot(time=None, **kwargs) load(...).plot(...) line(), lines(), spectrogram(), … PlotStack panels info(), schema(), guide(), example() Descriptions and definitions plan(time) Source files or dataset IDs to be read

Place source files under store.raw_path("<name>", "<provider>", ...) with the provider's layout, and after retrieval record the URL and checksum with store.register_raw_file(...). Write downloads to a temporary file and replace atomically, keeping the previous file on failure. When caching derived products, derive variant_id from settings and input content and register with managed=True.

docs.title: 4. Support Pipeline (when needed)
docs.text:
Subclass PipelineBackend and override only the operations you support. The endpoint's pipeline(time) returns a Pipeline with this backend attached.

from sopran.core.pipeline import Pipeline, PipelineBackend

class MyBackend(PipelineBackend):
    def scan_pipeline(self, pipeline: Pipeline):
        ...   # return a polars.LazyFrame; stream(partition="day") is split from it automatically

    def run_pipeline(self, pipeline: Pipeline, *, mode, run_id, resume, only_failed, on_error, download):
        ...   # return a PipelineResult

Operations that are not overridden raise PipelineError. The PACE implementation is in src/sopran/missions/kaguya/pipeline.py.

docs.title: 5. Add documentation and tests
docs.text:
• Write the description returned by guide() in the package's README.md (English) and README.ja.md, and pass the public documentation URL to GuidePage(url=...).
  • Add a page under Data in the public documentation, following the template in Writing Documentation.
  • Import optional dependencies lazily on the path that uses them and add them to an extra; tests/test_project_metadata.py checks that extras match actual imports.
  • Test units, the distinction between missing values and zeros, half-open time ranges, and cache keys with synthetic data or fixtures.

docs.title: License And Porting
docs.text: SOPRAN's original code and documentation are released under the Apache License 2.0 (LICENSE, NOTICE). Project metadata, LICENSE, NOTICE, and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md are kept consistent.

docs.title: Porting SPEDAS behavior
docs.text:
SOPRAN follows IDL SPEDAS behavior for KAGUYA processing and similar work. No SPEDAS or PySPEDAS source is currently copied.

Subject Policy New SOPRAN code Apache-2.0 SPEDAS behavior Used to understand specifications and as a reference for agreement tests MIT-licensed SPEDAS and PySPEDAS routines May be ported. Copied or derivative parts keep the original copyright and MIT permission notice, with SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 AND MIT and their source GPL or NASA Open Source Agreement external components Not copied into the core package without a separate license review External data The provider's terms are recorded in dataset manifests

Ported files state the upstream routine, the upstream commit or release, and whether they are a clean reimplementation, a behavior-compatible rewrite, or a direct translation. Where possible, implementations are rebuilt in Python and Rust from public instrument specifications, papers, and golden tests. When compared with SPEDAS, the SPEDAS version and routine path are recorded. Third-party fragments are kept separate so they can be audited, replaced, or removed without changing the public API.

The license findings and the full policy are in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
SOPRAN is published to PyPI from GitHub Actions with Trusted Publishing; no long-lived API tokens are used.

Item Value Workflow .github/workflows/publish.yml Trigger Pushing a v* tag PyPI project sopran GitHub environment pypi Authentication GitHub OIDC and PyPI Trusted Publisher

docs.title: What the workflow does
docs.text:
1. Checks that version in pyproject.toml, __version__ in src/sopran/__init__.py, and the tag without v agree.
  2. Builds the source distribution with python -m build --sdist.
  3. Builds CPython 3.11–3.14 wheels for Linux, Windows, and macOS with cibuildwheel.
  4. Checks that sopran._native imports from each wheel.
  5. Checks metadata and README with python -m twine check dist/*.
  6. Uploads to PyPI with pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
# 1. set version in pyproject.toml and __version__ in src/sopran/__init__.py to the same value (e.g. 0.1.0)

# 2. commit and tag
git add pyproject.toml src/sopran/__init__.py
git commit -m "Release v0.1.0"
git tag v0.1.0

# 3. pushing the tag starts the publish workflow
git push origin main
git push origin v0.1.0

If the three versions disagree, the build job fails. Before each release, review the experiments as described in Experimental.

docs.title: Checks beforehand
docs.text:
python -m build --sdist --wheel
python -m twine check dist/*

# try building a wheel for the current OS
python -m pip install "cibuildwheel>=2.23,<3"
python -m cibuildwheel --output-dir wheelhouse

docs.title: First-time PyPI setup
docs.text:
If the sopran project does not exist on PyPI yet, create a pending publisher under Publishing in your PyPI account.

PyPI field Value Project name sopran Owner Nkzono99 Repository name sopran Workflow name publish.yml Environment name pypi

A pending publisher does not reserve the name. If a project with the same name is registered before the first upload, it becomes invalid.

docs.title: Setup And Checks
docs.text: How to set up an environment for changing SOPRAN code or documentation, and which checks to run afterwards. For installing as a user, see Installation.

docs.title: Create the environment
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Nkzono99/sopran.git
cd sopran
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e ".[dev,full,docs]"     # on Windows use .venv\Scripts\python.exe

pip install -e . also builds the Rust extension sopran._native into the source tree. After changing only Rust code, rebuild the extension with:

python -m maturin develop --release
python -c "import sopran._native as native; print(native.__file__)"

sopran-env-check --native checks the build tools. maturin develop replaces the extension inside the source tree, so when long-running jobs use the same tree, work in a separate copy with a separate virtual environment.

docs.title: Check commands
docs.text:
Run from the repository root with the virtual environment's python, choosing the checks relevant to your change.

Target Command Related tests / all tests python -m pytest -q tests/test_omni.py / python -m pytest -q Syntax, lint, types python -m compileall -q src / python -m ruff check src tests / python -m mypy src Rust cargo test -p sopran-native / cargo fmt --all --check Schema changes python -m sopran.schema_docs --check docs/ja/reference/schemas.md / python -m sopran.schema_docs --language en --check docs/en/reference/schemas.md Documentation changes python -m mkdocs build --strict Connection to remote archives python -m pytest -m network / sopran-env-check --sources

Tests rely mostly on synthetic data and fixtures. They do not assume an IDL installation; comparisons with SPEDAS behavior use reference specifications, synthetic data, and existing real data.

The regular tests never reach the network: tests/conftest.py blocks connections to anything but loopback, and download paths are tested by replacing urlopen and similar functions. Tests that do reach remote servers are marked @pytest.mark.network. They are deselected by default and run only with -m network.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: Workflow Contents .github/workflows/ci.yml Installs [dev,kaguya,moon,viz,docs,experimental] and runs pytest, compileall, the schema page check, ruff, and mypy .github/workflows/sources.yml Every Monday and on manual dispatch, checks the connection to the remote archives with sopran-env-check --sources .github/workflows/docs.yml Builds the documentation with mkdocs build --strict and publishes to GitHub Pages from the main branch .github/workflows/publish.yml On v* tags, builds the sdist and wheels for each OS and CPython 3.11–3.14 and publishes to PyPI (Release)

docs.title: Supercomputers
docs.text: Environment setup and job templates for the Kyoto University supercomputer are in scripts/hpc/kyoto/. See ER Full-Period Batch for their use.

docs.title: Experimental APIs
docs.text:
sopran.experimental holds research models and analysis steps that are organized well enough to try on other data. Unlike the regular instrument APIs, names, defaults, and storage formats may change or disappear without notice, and the physical correctness of results is not guaranteed.

python -m pip install -e ".[kaguya,viz,experimental]"

import sopran alone does not load any experiment. Import the module you need explicitly.

docs.title: Boundary with the regular API
docs.text:
PACE, LMAG, and LRS retrieval, calibration, native bins, coordinate transforms, the Store, PlotStack, and Moon maps stay at the regular entry points. ER estimates are not instrument observations, so there is no spn.kaguya.er entry point, and ER types and functions are not re-exported under spn.

Dependencies point one way, from experiments to the regular API. The regular API never imports experiments, and tests/test_experimental_boundary.py checks this boundary. When saving experimental results in the Store, use dataset IDs that start with experimental. so they never mix with regular products.

Experiments that used to live in sopran.analysis.electron_reflection, sopran.analysis.waves, sopran.missions.kaguya.er*, and sopran.bodies.moon.svm3d have moved to the places above. No aliases for the old names remain.

docs.title: Promote, keep, or retire
docs.text:
The purpose, open questions, promotion requirements, and last review date of each experiment are tracked in src/sopran/experimental/README.md. They are reviewed before each release; experiments promoted to the regular API get types, units, sources, regression tests, and a stated validation scope.

Runs over specific periods, comparison figures, interpretations of results, and literature surveys are recorded in each study's working directory (working/), not in the public documentation. This section covers only how to use the experimental APIs and their limits.

docs.title: Pitch-Angle Spectra In The dHT Frame
docs.text: sopran.experimental.kaguya.dht moves each KAGUYA ESA look velocity into the de Hoffmann–Teller (dHT) frame, in which the motional electric field of the solar-wind flow vanishes, and recomputes pitch angle and energy from there. It is meant for reading the electron distribution under the condition that the loss-cone boundary is fixed to the lunar surface. Records whose field is nearly tangent to the surface have no dHT velocity, so the usable sample is much smaller than the plain distribution. Keep the plain pitch-angle spectrum as the reference and use the dHT version as a comparison.

docs.title: Velocity convention
docs.text:
The order fixed by the September 2026 lunarsat validation (20-minute interval, 59 records) is implemented as is.

Step Content 1 Take \(\boldsymbol V_\mathrm{GSE}\) from the OMNI HRO 5-minute sample whose lunar arrival time is nearest the record (within omni_tolerance_seconds) 2 Restore the Earth orbital aberration that NASA removed, once, as +29.8 km/s in \(V_y\) (restore_omni_aberration) 3 Rotate GSE→J2000 with the Sun direction at the OMNI epoch, then J2000→MOON_ME at the record time 4 Subtract the Moon's geocentric velocity and build the HT velocity \(\boldsymbol H_M=\boldsymbol u_M-\frac{\boldsymbol u_M\cdot\boldsymbol n}{\boldsymbol B\cdot\boldsymbol n}\boldsymbol B\) with the local radial as the normal 5 Subtract the spacecraft's selenocentric velocity and rotate into the look frame (default SELENE_M_SPACECRAFT) 6 Subtract this boost from every look velocity and recompute the pitch angle \(\alpha'\) and energy \(E'\)

The lunar arrival time is \(t_\mathrm{arrival}=t_\mathrm{OMNI}+(R_E\,\mathrm{BSN}_x-x_\mathrm{Moon,GSE})/V_\mathrm{sw}\); arrival_shift="none" disables it. Moon and spacecraft velocities come from SPICE spkezr (DE421 and the SELENE SPK) in inertial axes, and only 3×3 pxform rotations are applied.

Records with \(|\boldsymbol B\cdot\boldsymbol n|/|\boldsymbol B|\) below min_abs_b_normal_fraction (default 0.15) are dropped as field_tangent. In the April 2026 lunarsat full-period runs the dHT branch kept about 27% of the non-dHT fits.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import numpy as np
import sopran as spn
from sopran.experimental.kaguya.dht import DhtSettings, dht_pitch_angle_spectrum
from sopran.frames import FrameContext
from sopran.missions.kaguya.geometry import lmag_position, lmag_position_gse
from sopran.missions.kaguya.spice import selene_spice_kernels

kg = spn.Kaguya()
time = spn.period("2008-04-02T08:20", "2008-04-02T08:50")
calibration = kg.esa1.load_calibration()
esa1 = kg.esa1.load(time, calibration=calibration)
lmag = kg.lmag.load(time)
omni = spn.omni.hro.load(spn.period("2008-04-02T07:00", "2008-04-02T09:00"))
frames = FrameContext(spice_kernels=selene_spice_kernels(kg.store, time), default_backend="spiceypy")

result = dht_pitch_angle_spectrum(
    pace=esa1.pace,
    time=time,
    calibration=calibration,
    magnetic_field=lmag.magnetic_field,
    position=lmag_position(lmag),
    position_gse=lmag_position_gse(lmag),
    omni=omni,
    frame_context=frames,
    energy_edges_eV=np.geomspace(20.0, 1500.0, 10),
    pitch_bins=16,
    settings=DhtSettings(),
)
result.spectrum            # counts on time x energy band x pitch_angle (SopranArray)
result.frame.coverage()    # {"records": ..., "ok": ..., "field_tangent": ..., "omni_missing": ...}
result.frame.to_pandas()   # per-record boost, |B.n|/|B|, OMNI time offset

Shifted energies fall into the energy_edges_eV bands, so every record shares one grid. The exposure coordinate is the look response summed with the factor \((E/E')^2\), so counts / exposure approximates the differential energy flux in the dHT frame (Liouville's theorem). exposure_unshifted is the plain sum, look_samples the number of looks per cell, and shifted_energy_mean_eV and unshifted_pitch_mean_deg the cell means.

The parts are available on their own: frame_velocity() gives the boost and diagnostics per record, shift_looks() the per-look shift, dht_tangential_velocity() the HT velocity and lunar_arrival_times() the arrival times.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Only the motional electric field is removed; electrostatic potentials are not treated. DhtSettings.look_sign treats the look direction as the particle velocity direction (+1).
  • Reasons for dropped records stay in frame.status (ok, omni_missing, geometry_missing, field_tangent, spice_failed). Report coverage() before plotting or fitting.
  • The SPICE kernels must cover Earth, Moon and Sun (DE421), the spacecraft (SELENE SPK), the lunar orientation (MOON_ME) and the attitude (CK); selene_spice_kernels provides them.
  • Sources: OMNI HRO documentation Appendix 4 (aberration), NAIF spkezr/pxform, lunarsat working/kgy-er/notes/er-dht-velocity-convention-2026-09-27.md.

docs.title: ER Full-Period Batch
docs.text:
sopran.experimental.kaguya.er_batch is a CLI that runs finite-bin fits and \(R_m\) profiles over the full mission on saved paired distributions. The same commands run on a workstation and as Slurm array jobs on the Kyoto University supercomputer. Inputs and outputs are Store datasets split into daily Parquet, so rsync can move them as they are.

Dataset Layer variant Contents experimental.kaguya.er.paired_distributions features Input build name Folded counts, exposures, and window records per 16 s window; one shard per day experimental.kaguya.er.finite_bin_fits models Run name Fits, profiles, and candidates per window; one shard per day

Commands take the form python -m sopran.experimental.kaguya.er_batch [--data-root ROOT] <command>. Without --data-root, the Store from SOPRAN_DATA_ROOT (or the SOPRAN configuration) is used. It needs the experimental and kaguya extras.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
export-catalog → verify-inputs → prepare → run (parallel, resumable) → status → finalize → compare
Command Action export-catalog --catalog PATH --input-variant V [--workers N] Convert a SQLite catalog to daily shards; existing days are skipped verify-inputs --input-variant V Check input shard checksums after a transfer prepare --input-variant V --run-variant R [--groups G] [--fit-setting name=JSON] Freeze settings, inputs, and code and environment hashes in run.json run --run-variant R [--group i \| --days D...] [--workers N] Fit the given days; only unfinished days are processed status --run-variant R Show completed days and heartbeats finalize --run-variant R Recompute checksums of completed shards and register them in the Store catalog compare --run-variant R --reference FILE... Compare objectives, \(B_\mathrm{eff}\), and candidates of the same windows with daily Parquet from another run

docs.title: Preparing inputs
docs.text: Inputs are either converted from a SQLite catalog of per-window paired distributions, or built from source data with the SOPRAN parts below.

docs.title: Converting a SQLite catalog
docs.text:
The catalog has one table, windows.

Column Type Contents sample_id TEXT ID of the 16 s window day TEXT UTC day (YYYY-MM-DD) record TEXT Window record (JSON); time, b_sc_nT, affected_side, field_connection_status, field_radial_abs_cosine_min, magnetic_direction_max_deviation_deg, and reason are read maps BLOB .npz; NULL for windows without a distribution

maps holds the arrays in FLOAT_ARRAYS and BOOL_ARRAYS. Folded arrays are energy × pitch_folded, and global_* arrays are energy × pitch.

python -m sopran.experimental.kaguya.er_batch --data-root /path/to/sopran_data export-catalog \
  --catalog /path/to/catalog.sqlite --input-variant <build> --workers 3

The conversion moves folded counts, exposures, fit_valid, and pair_observed, plus all-pitch counts, exposures, and energy and pitch edges, from each window's npz into row-major flattened list columns. It also checks that every array is representable losslessly as float64 or bool. Derived quantities of earlier fits (observed_log_ratio, fitted_log_ratio, beam_ratio) are not carried over. The window record (JSON) and the sha256 of record plus npz (source_sha256) are kept, and days.json lists window counts, distribution counts, and checksums for every day, including days without input.

docs.title: Building from source data with SOPRAN parts
docs.text:
Parts are also available to build input shards from source data without a SQLite catalog. Their defaults match the rules of the September 2026 full-period run (halekas_mission_v1). Assembling a full-period run (parallel days, resuming, logs) is left to your own script.

Stage Part Native records and LMAG geometry for one day KaguyaErInstrument(mission).native_records(day) Aggregation into 16 s windows and diagnostics er_windows.calendar_windows, window_record, window_input_diagnostic Connection screening with SVM3D moon.connection.trace_connection, classify_connection (ConnectionPolicy) Paired distribution er_windows.window_pitch_records → electron_reflection.maps.build_paired_map Writing and registration er_batch.window_input_row → er_batch.write_input_days 
import numpy as np
import sopran as spn
from sopran.experimental.electron_reflection.maps import build_paired_map
from sopran.experimental.kaguya import er_batch
from sopran.experimental.kaguya.er import KaguyaErInstrument
from sopran.experimental.kaguya.er_windows import (
    calendar_windows, usable_record_indices, window_input_diagnostic,
    window_pitch_records, window_record,
)
from sopran.experimental.moon.connection import (
    classify_connection, trace_connection, unconnected_window,
)
from sopran.experimental.moon.svm3d import SVM3DShellGrid

day = spn.day("2008-02-10")
records = KaguyaErInstrument(spn.Kaguya(download="never")).native_records(day)
usable = np.unique(np.concatenate(
    [usable_record_indices(a, np.arange(records.times.size)) for a in records.arrays.values()]
))
traces = trace_connection(
    SVM3DShellGrid.load("svm3d_shell.npz"),
    records.position_km[usable], records.magnetic_field_nT[usable],
)
connection = classify_connection(
    traces, records.times[usable].astype("datetime64[s]").astype(int) // 16
)

rows = []
for window_id, indices in calendar_windows(records.times, day):
    record = window_record(window_id, indices, records)
    record.update(connection.get(window_id, unconnected_window()))
    record["joint_input_diagnostic"] = window_input_diagnostic(indices, records.arrays)
    usable_here = any(usable_record_indices(a, indices).size for a in records.arrays.values())
    reason = "no_records" if not indices.size else None if usable_here else "no_usable_geometry"
    if reason is None and not record["connection_eligible"]:
        reason = "connection_" + record["field_connection_status"]
    if reason:
        record["reason"] = reason
    maps = None if reason else build_paired_map(window_pitch_records(records, indices))
    rows.append(er_batch.window_input_row(record, maps))
er_batch.write_input_days(spn.Store(), "<build>", {"2008-02-10": rows})

The parts follow these rules.

  • window_record derives the maximum field-direction deviation from the LMAG samples in the window, and field_radial_abs_cosine_min from the cosine between \(B\) and \(r\) at the record times.
  • build_paired_map orients each record so the affected side is at low pitch angles, distributes it onto a 20–1500 eV, 24 energy × 16 pitch grid by bin overlap, sums counts and exposures, and folds into affected and reference. fit_valid marks the range where both sides of the pair have positive exposure and counts, with at least three cells per energy row.
  • Connection screening traces the SVM3D field plus a uniform residual in 0.5 km steps, stopping at 6.1 km altitude and at most 1000 km. Windows where the inward trace reaches the shell, the opposite one does not, and the side does not change within the window are model_connected.

docs.title: Freezing and running
docs.text:
prepare records in run.json the settings (defaults of FiniteBinFitSettings() plus --fit-setting overrides) and the input catalog checksum. --min-fit-energy E removes rows whose centre energy is below E eV from the fitted cells and records it as config.min_fit_energy_eV. It also records the sha256 of the fitting code and the Rust extension, and the versions of Python, numpy, scipy, and polars. run compares these with the current environment at startup and stops on any difference. To change settings, prepare a new run name.

run processes days one at a time and spreads each day's windows over worker processes (spawn). Workers pin OMP_NUM_THREADS and similar variables to 1. --workers defaults to the allocated CPUs (affinity on Linux), and 0 runs in process. Every 256 windows are saved to work/<day>/part-*.parquet; when a day finishes, shards/day=<day>.parquet and days/<day>.json are written. Rerunning skips completed days and never recomputes saved parts. Creating a file named STOP in the run directory makes every invocation save and exit after its current window. Each invocation writes only its own days' files, so array jobs may run at the same time. --groups G splits days into G groups balanced by distribution count, and run --group i processes group i.

Each window is fitted with the default count-likelihood settings. Profiles are computed only for windows that meet the geometry conditions (\(B_\mathrm{sc} > 0\), field-direction deviation ≤ 20°, angle to radial < 80°, model_connected) and have no field_flags. Profiles use 13 points over \(R_m\) ±1 dex and give the 95% interval and minimum_fit. Column meanings are in the schema.json written by finalize.

docs.title: Running on the Kyoto University supercomputer
docs.text:
Scripts are in scripts/hpc/kyoto/. Kyoto's Slurm is extended: resources are requested with --rsc p=PROCS:t=THREADS:c=CORES:m=MEMORY, the -p queue is mandatory, and programs start with srun (KUDPC batch processing manual). The templates follow this format, but confirm queue names, limits, and array-job environment variables in a first pilot.

  1. Move the data. Input datasets are managed and thus in the default list, but here only the inputs are selected by name.

    sopran-store --data-root /path/to/sopran_data sync-list \
  --dataset experimental.kaguya.er.paired_distributions > files.txt
rsync -av --delay-updates --files-from=files.txt /path/to/sopran_data/ <host>:$SOPRAN_DATA_ROOT/

    After the transfer, run sopran-store rebuild and verify-inputs on the destination.

  2. Build the environment on a login node. Clone SOPRAN with git and run the following; it installs uv and Rust under $HOME and builds SOPRAN (non-editable) into a version-pinned venv.

    SOPRAN_SRC=$HOME/src/sopran ENV_ROOT=/LARGE0/grXXXXX/$USER/sopran-env \
  bash scripts/hpc/kyoto/setup_env.sh

    Alternatively, install the manylinux x86_64 wheel built by CI (publish.yml) with --no-deps.

  3. Check and freeze on the login node.

    source $ENV_ROOT/venv/bin/activate
export SOPRAN_DATA_ROOT=/LARGE0/grXXXXX/$USER/sopran_data
python -m sopran.experimental.kaguya.er_batch verify-inputs --input-variant <build>
python -m sopran.experimental.kaguya.er_batch prepare --input-variant <build> \
  --run-variant <run> --groups 16

  4. Check agreement with a pilot. Create a separate run with --days set to one day already completed locally, and run one task (-a 0). Transfer that day's Parquet from the local run and compare with compare. Linux and Windows implement exponential and logarithm functions differently, so exact agreement is not expected; check that relative objective differences are small and candidates agree.

  5. Submit production. Edit -p, -t, --rsc, and -a 0-(G-1) in scripts/hpc/kyoto/er_fit.sbatch, export ENV_ROOT, SOPRAN_DATA_ROOT, and RUN_VARIANT, and sbatch. Tasks that time out continue where they stopped when resubmitted with the same command.

  6. Collect results. Confirm completion with status and register with finalize. Bring results back with the list from sopran-store sync-list --dataset experimental.kaguya.er.finite_bin_fits --variant <run>, then run sopran-store rebuild locally.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: tests/test_er_batch.py checks that conversion is lossless, the prepare → run → finalize → scan flow, resuming from parts, STOP, rejection after code changes, balanced day groups, and agreement between spawn workers and in-process runs. Comparisons on real data use compare, and their results are recorded per run in working/.

docs.title: ER Model Definitions
docs.text: This page defines the model, objective, numerics, and quality checks of the two estimators used in Electron Reflectometry. Both take ElectronReflectionCounts over energy × folded pitch angle (affected and reference counts and exposures).

docs.title: finite-bin model
docs.text:
from sopran.experimental.electron_reflection import (
    FiniteBinFitSettings, FiniteBinObservation, fit_finite_bin_distribution, profile_mirror_ratio,
)

observation = FiniteBinObservation.from_counts(
    counts, energy_edges_eV=energy_edges, pitch_edges_deg=folded_pitch_edges,
)
result = fit_finite_bin_distribution(observation, settings=FiniteBinFitSettings())
profile = profile_mirror_ratio(observation, result)

docs.title: Model equation
docs.text:
The incident flux, integrated over solid angle, is multiplied by the reflectance and a beam, moved by the angular transport \(D_\mathrm{out}\), and mapped back to observed ratios through ideal bin responses uniform in log energy and pitch angle.

\[ N_\mathrm{out} = D_\mathrm{out}\left\{ s\left[\rho + (1-\rho)P_0\right] N_\mathrm{in} + N_\mathrm{beam} \right\}, \qquad \sin^2\alpha_c = \frac{1 + \Delta U / E}{R_m}. \] Symbol Name in result.parameters Meaning \(R_m\) mirror_ratio Magnetic mirror ratio; \(B_\mathrm{eff} = R_m B_\mathrm{sc}\) (result.effective_field_nT) \(\Delta U\) delta_u_eV Potential difference, surface minus spacecraft (eV) \(\rho\) bottom_ratio Relative level inside the loss cone; inside is \(s\rho\), outside \(s\) \(s\) scale Overall scale sigma_deg Diffusion strength of \(D_\mathrm{out}\) \(\phi\) concentration Beta-binomial concentration \(\alpha_c\) Pitch angle of the loss-cone boundary \(P_0\) Reflection indicator: 1 outside the boundary, 0 inside

Search ranges are set with mirror_ratio_bounds, delta_u_bounds_eV, bottom_ratio_bounds, scale_bounds, sigma_bounds_deg, and concentration_bounds in FiniteBinFitSettings.

The beam is enabled by default and disabled with beam_enabled=False. There are four shapes combining log-energy widths 0.15 and 0.30 with pitch widths 10° and 20°. The amplitude is chosen continuously within beam_amplitude_bounds (default 0.25–8) by a one-dimensional golden-section search per shape at every evaluation. By default (beam_energy="delta_u") the centre energy is \(-\Delta U\) and the beam is active only for \(\Delta U < 0\), following Halekas et al. (2008, 2011) for secondary electrons accelerated from a negatively charged surface. With beam_energy="free", the centre is fitted within beam_energy_bounds_eV (default 20–200 eV) as a seventh parameter (FiniteBinParameters.beam_energy_eV, starting at 45 eV), and the beam is active whatever the sign of \(\Delta U\), so that a low-energy excess unrelated to \(\Delta U\) does not produce a spurious negative \(\Delta U\). In results, beam_template is 0 for no beam, otherwise 1 + 2*energy_index + pitch_index; the amplitude is beam_amplitude and the centre beam_energy_eV (\(-\Delta U\) for delta_u).

A known efficiency ratio is added to the model ratio as the observation's model_offset_dex (log10 of the affected/reference efficiency ratio). scale_prior_sigma_dex places a zero-centered Gaussian prior on \(\log_{10}s\) (count losses only). Together with the offset, it moves the prior center to a calibration value.

docs.title: Angular transport \(D_\mathrm{out}\)
docs.text:
Enable it with FiniteBinFitSettings(angular_transport="out"); the default "none" is diagonal (no transport).

result.d_out[j_out, j_in] is the probability of moving from a source bin to a destination bin, and each column sums to 1. Its axis edges are result.transport_pitch_edges_deg; use 100 * result.d_out to display percentages. It acts after reflection and the beam and never mixes energies. It is axisymmetric diffusion with no-flux boundaries at 0° and 90° of the folded hemisphere, which keeps an isotropic flux stationary. sigma_deg is a diffusion parameter that matches the RMS direction change in the small-angle limit; for large values it is not the simple Gaussian standard deviation of pitch-angle differences. Zero reproduces the diagonal case.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
loss Observable Use "beta_binomial" (default) Affected counts given affected + reference trials Main analysis; systematic overdispersion is absorbed by the concentration \(\phi\) "binomial" Same Comparison assuming statistical errors only "huber" (default 0.1 dex) \(\log_{10}(a/r)\) Flux-only inputs, comparison with earlier analyses "squared" \(\log_{10}(a/r)\) Comparison

Count losses treat the affected count \(a\) as binomial with \(n = a + r\) trials. The affected probability is \(q = \lambda/(1+\lambda)\) with \(\lambda = x\,10^{c}R\), where \(R\) is the model ratio, \(x\) the affected/reference exposure ratio, and \(c\) model_offset_dex. The beta-binomial has mean \(q\) and concentration \(\phi\), estimated jointly with the other parameters. objective_sum is the \(-2\log L\) difference from the saturated binomial likelihood (the deviance), so differences between two fits read on a χ² scale. Count losses need an observation with counts (created with from_counts).

The Huber objective of a residual \(r\) is \(r^2\) for \(|r| \le 0.1\) and \(0.2|r| - 0.01\) otherwise. objective_sum and the per-cell objective_mean are returned. root_mean_square_error_dex is computed separately from squared residuals and is distinct from the objective value.

docs.title: Cells used in the fit
docs.text:
from_counts defaults to selection="total" and min_counts=1, keeping cells with \(a + r \ge 1\). Cells with \(a = 0\) enter the objective as information from inside the loss cone. selection="paired", min_counts=5 is the earlier selection that requires at least five counts on both sides. Because it selects on affected counts, cells deep in the loss cone drop out and \(\rho\) is biased upward. On synthetic counts with true \(\rho = 0.15\), paired + Huber gave 0.18–0.6 and total + beta-binomial gave 0.15.

With either selection, only energies with at least three pitch angles and exposure ratios between 0.01 and 100 are fitted. Log ratios use a pseudocount of 0.5 and serve RMSE and figures. Instrument calibration and potential corrections happen before this fit, and the incident flux keeps relative values across pitch angles within each energy.

Missing incident bins are interpolated in log flux within the same energy, with the nearest value at the ends. Interpolated bins are returned in interpolated_incident_bins, and the missing cells themselves are not added to the objective. Interpolated incident flux flows into observed cells through \(D_\mathrm{out}\), so many gaps make input assumptions matter. Reconstructions for unused energy rows stay NaN.

docs.title: Numerics
docs.text: Reflection boundaries and beams are evaluated with composite 17-point Gauss quadrature, and each pitch bin is split into 8 by default. The search uses seeded differential evolution (35 candidates, 180 generations, 2 seeds) and bounded Nelder–Mead (up to 650 iterations). When starts is omitted, Nelder–Mead also starts from 12 points: \(R_m\) = 1.2, 2, 5, 20 and \(\Delta U\) = −50, 0, +50 eV, because differential evolution alone missed the best minimum in 2 of 7 KAGUYA windows. Everything from the response to the optimization runs in Rust, with no Python callbacks and no implicit fallback to Python.

docs.title: Quality checks
docs.text:
local_converged reports local solver termination, and at_bounds that a free parameter sits at its search bound. field_unconstrained is True when any of the following field_flags is set.

Flag Condition no_contrast \(\rho \ge 0.99\) barrier_unobserved All fitted cells lie on one side of the boundary field_at_search_bound \(R_m\) at its search bound boundary_rows_insufficient Fewer energy rows with cells on both sides of the boundary than min_boundary_rows (default 3) loss_cone_unsupported loss_cone_delta_bic ≤ 0 with a count loss

loss_cone_delta_objective is the objective difference between two models that allow free levels per energy row: no loss cone (\(\rho = 1\)) and the fitted loss cone, with the same beam. A step only in energy is explained by both, so this difference measures whether pitch-angle structure is needed. loss_cone_delta_bic subtracts \(k\ln N\), where \(k\) is the number of free parameters among \(R_m\), \(\rho\), and \(\Delta U\). On real data a certain fraction of windows is loss_cone_unsupported, and the fraction is higher for solutions with \(R_m \le 1\).

docs.title: Profile intervals
docs.text:
No flags is not proof of identifiability, so adopt field values through profile_mirror_ratio. It fixes \(R_m\) on a grid (default ±1 dex, 21 points) and re-optimizes the other parameters from nearby solutions. With count losses, \(\Delta\)objective ≤ 3.84 defines the 95% interval, with ends interpolated between grid points.

Result Meaning interval_nT 95% interval of \(B_\mathrm{eff}\) interval_bounded=False The interval reached the edge of the grid improved_minimum=True The fit missed a better minimum, returned as minimum_fit
