Results of evaluate with fixed parameters have local_converged False.

docs.title: Fixing parameters
docs.text: Equal lower and upper bounds fix a parameter. For example, to fix \(B_\mathrm{eff}\) to a regional mean field and refit \(\Delta U\) and the rest, use mirror_ratio_bounds=(area_mean_nT / b_sc, area_mean_nT / b_sc). bottom_ratio_bounds=(0.1, 0.1) and scale_bounds=(1, 1) compare finite-bin at the fixed 0.1/1 levels.

docs.title: Halekas model
docs.text:
from sopran.experimental.electron_reflection import HalekasFitSettings, fit_halekas_distribution

result = fit_halekas_distribution(counts, settings=HalekasFitSettings())

Halekas minimizes squared residuals of exposure-corrected natural-log ratios. Cells with \(a + r\) below min_cell_total_counts (default 1) are dropped, because empty cells get a ratio of 1 from the pseudocount and would look like the loss cone is absent. root_mean_square_error is in natural-log units; divide by np.log(10) before comparing with a dex RMSE on the same input and mask.

edge_transition Model and search "hard" (default) Binary distribution with fixed backscatter (default 0.1) and outer level 1, evaluated at bin centers; grid search and refinement over \(R_m\) and \(\Delta U\) "probit" Same levels with a boundary width; L-BFGS-B starting from the hard solution and others

Free bottom, scale, beams, and \(D_\mathrm{out}\) belong to finite-bin. The probit width (boundary smoothing) and \(D_\mathrm{out}\) (transport between angles) are different parameters. When comparing RMSE, match units and masks, and do not compare the Halekas Gaussian BIC with Huber values directly.

docs.title: For comparison: the robust mirror-transmission model
docs.text:
from sopran.experimental.electron_reflection.mirror_transmission import (
    MirrorTransmissionSettings, fit_mirror_transmission, fit_mirror_transmission_variants, ratio_from_counts,
)

energy, pitch, ratio, b_sc = ratio_from_counts(counts)      # affected/reference rate ratio
fit = fit_mirror_transmission(energy, pitch, ratio, b_sc, settings=MirrorTransmissionSettings())
variants = fit_mirror_transmission_variants(energy, pitch, ratio, b_sc)   # four nested models

A comparison estimator ported from lunarsat (robust_mirror_transmission_log_ratio_v1). The natural log of the ratio is modelled as \(a_j + A_j\,P(E_j,\alpha_k)\) with per-energy baseline \(a_j\) and contrast \(A_j\) nuisance terms; only the boundary and width shared across energy are estimated.

\[ \sin^2\alpha_c = p_0\left(1 + \frac{\Delta U + \beta_1 s^2 + \beta_2 s^3}{E - U_\mathrm{sc}}\right),\quad s = \frac{E_*}{E - U_\mathrm{sc} + E_*},\qquad P = \Phi\!\left(\frac{\ln\sin^2\alpha - \ln\sin^2\alpha_c}{\sigma(E)}\right) \] Symbol Name Meaning \(p_0\) p0 High-energy asymptote of \(B_\mathrm{sc}/B_\mathrm{eff}\); b_eff_nT = b_sc_reference_nT / p0 \(\Delta U\) delta_u_eff_eV Potential term (fixed to 0 in mirror_only) \(\beta_1, \beta_2\) smooth_beta1_eV, smooth_beta2_eV Low-energy correction of smooth_low_energy; the high-energy limit is unchanged \(\sigma\) sigma_ln_b Log-width of the boundary; energy_broadened uses \(\sqrt{\sigma^2 + (U_w/(E+E_0))^2}\)

The loss is soft_l1 (robust_f_scale = 0.2) with scipy.optimize.least_squares. fit.success requires both optimiser convergence and a boundary inside \(0<\sin^2\alpha_c<1\); compare variants through the difference from no_edge_rmse_log (row means only) and through aic_log/bic_log. Relative to the lunarsat version only the initial guess (per-row threshold crossings) is simplified; model, bounds and loss are the same. Its input and objective differ from the finite-bin count likelihood, so the numbers are not compared directly.

docs.title: Electron Reflectometry
docs.text:
Electron reflectometry (ER) uses the electron energy–pitch-angle distribution measured on the spacecraft to infer where electrons heading toward the Moon were turned back (the reflection barrier). SOPRAN's experimental implementation fits the magnetic mirror ratio \(R_m\) and the potential difference \(\Delta U\) to the boundary of the loss cone in the pitch-angle distribution.

Limits of interpretation

A numerically converged fit does not mean the lunar surface field was measured. \(B_\mathrm{eff} = R_m B_\mathrm{sc}\) (nT) is an effective field describing the reflection boundary, not the crustal field vector. \(\Delta U\) is "surface potential − spacecraft potential" (eV), not the absolute surface potential. Decide whether to adopt a field value from the quality flags and profile intervals described below.

docs.title: Choosing a method
docs.text:
There are two estimators: finite-bin and Halekas.

Purpose Method and settings Main analysis finite-bin with the beta-binomial count likelihood (default); enable angular transport \(D_\mathrm{out}\) as needed Deciding whether to adopt a field profile_mirror_ratio intervals and field_flags Flux-only inputs, comparison with earlier analyses finite-bin with loss="huber" (0.1 dex) Comparison with a fixed 0.1 reflectance and outer level 1 Halekas

Model equations, objectives, and flag definitions are in ER Model Definitions.

docs.title: Estimating from KAGUYA data
docs.text:
import sopran as spn
from sopran.experimental.kaguya.er import KaguyaErInstrument
from sopran.experimental.electron_reflection import (
    FiniteBinFitSettings, FiniteBinObservation, HalekasFitSettings,
)

er = KaguyaErInstrument(spn.Kaguya())
pitch_counts = er.pitch_angle_spectrum(spn.day("2008-04-26"))

# magnetic_field and position are arrays or SopranArrays in the same frame
counts = er.paired_counts(
    pitch_counts, index=0, magnetic_field=magnetic_field, position=position,
)

observation = FiniteBinObservation.from_counts(
    counts, energy_edges_eV=energy_edges, pitch_edges_deg=folded_pitch_edges,
)
result = er.effective_field.fit_finite_bin(
    observation, settings=FiniteBinFitSettings(angular_transport="out"),
)
profile = er.effective_field.profile_finite_bin(observation, result)

comparison = er.effective_field.fit_halekas(counts, settings=HalekasFitSettings())

docs.title: Preparing inputs
docs.text:
KaguyaErInstrument shares ESA loading and calibration, LMAG loading with margins, and SPICE setup between its two loading entry points. pitch_angle_spectra(..., align=False) returns pitch-angle spectra that keep each sensor's own times.

paired_counts builds an ElectronReflectionCounts (energy × folded pitch angle) that pairs 0–90° with 90–180° for one sample.

  • The hemisphere of electrons coming back from the surface (after reflection) is "affected", and the hemisphere of electrons heading toward the surface (incident) is "reference". When +B points away from the Moon, low pitch angles are affected; otherwise high pitch angles are. affected_side="low" or "high" sets it explicitly.
  • Pass the calibrated, actual bin edges to finite-bin as energy_edges_eV and pitch_edges_deg; edges are never inferred from centers.
  • Exposure is taken from an explicit value, then the spectrum's coordinates, then equal exposure. An explicit value must broadcast to energy × pitch angle of the selected sample. Assuming equal exposure is recorded in the input metadata.

Retrieval and calibration use the kaguya extra, estimation experimental, and plotting viz.

docs.title: Reading results
docs.text:
result.effective_field_nT       # B_eff
result.field_flags              # reasons the field is not constrained
result.field_unconstrained      # True when any field_flags is set
profile.interval_nT             # 95% interval from re-optimizing with R_m fixed

No flags does not mean the field is uniquely determined. Use the profile interval to decide, and check individually any result whose interval reaches the search range (interval_bounded=False) or where a better solution was found (improved_minimum=True). In windows where the count and Huber losses land in different minima, the count-loss profile interval may contain both. Judge identifiability by the interval width, not by the difference between point estimates.

docs.title: Saving results
docs.text: Estimates come back as typed dataclasses per method and are not saved to the Store automatically. Save them yourself together with the settings, inputs, masks, bins, and a code hash. For processing the full mission with fixed settings and code, see ER Full-Period Batch.

docs.title: Module layout
docs.text: Location Role electron_reflection/common.py Shared input type ElectronReflectionCounts, exposure validation, boundary formula mirror_boundary_sin2 electron_reflection/finite_bin.py finite-bin model, losses, loss-cone test, profiles electron_reflection/halekas.py Halekas model experimental/kaguya/er.py ESA1/ESA2, LMAG, and SPICE preparation, pitch-angle spectra, paired_counts, estimator calls experimental/kaguya/er_batch.py Full-period daily sharding, frozen settings, parallel fits, Store registration crates/sopran-native/src/finite_bin.rs finite-bin response, \(D_\mathrm{out}\), losses, and optimization (Rust)

docs.title: Retired estimators
docs.text: The paired-count beta-binomial estimator (its count likelihood merged into finite-bin loss on 2026-10-10), binary surface, joint, global-joint, incident, and integrated estimators, and their dedicated warm starts, likelihood scans, time series, catalogs, schemas, and evaluation helpers, have been removed. Use fit_finite_bin and fit_halekas instead of the old fit, fit_joint, fit_global_joint, fit_timeseries, and build. The former sopran-er-finite-bin JSONL CLI is also retired in favor of the PyO3 API. There are no compatibility aliases or fallbacks to old estimators. Previously saved data remains in the Store and can be read as regular datasets.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Target Tests finite-bin, \(D_\mathrm{out}\), losses (checked against scipy binomial and beta-binomial), count selection, loss-cone test, offset and prior, profile intervals, missing bins, fixed \(B_\mathrm{eff}\) tests/test_er_finite_bin.py Halekas hard/probit recovery, \(R_m<1\), search agreement test_electron_reflection.py, test_electron_reflection_subunity.py, test_halekas_search.py KAGUYA inputs, exposure, geometry, loading test_kaguya_er.py, test_kaguya_er_geometry.py, test_kaguya_pace.py The regular API does not load experiments test_experimental_boundary.py

docs.title: Field Models And Orbit Tools
docs.text:
Experimental tools for comparing ER results with field models and environment conditions. They return results and never write to the Store on their own.

Tool Module Purpose Test-particle orbits sopran.experimental.moon.test_particle Electron orbits in SVM3D plus a uniform external field (Boris, magnetic only) Closed-field islands sopran.experimental.moon.closure Connected components of closed cells on a grid Field residual and quiet baseline sopran.experimental.kaguya.field_residual Decomposition of observed minus model field; quiet-time median baseline Environment-response regression sopran.experimental.statistics.ridge Standardized ridge, track-grouped cross-validation, external-field gain

docs.title: Test-particle orbits
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from sopran.experimental.moon.svm3d import SVM3DShellGrid
from sopran.experimental.moon.test_particle import (
    TestParticleSettings, electron_velocity_me, trace_test_particles,
)

grid = SVM3DShellGrid.load("svm3d_shell_grid.npz")
r0 = np.array([[1737.4 + 100.0, 0.0, 0.0]])              # MOON_ME [km]
b_external = np.array([[2.0, -1.0, 4.0]])                  # uniform external field [nT]
b_local = b_external + grid.field_at(r0)
v0 = electron_velocity_me([200.0], [150.0], [0.0], b_local)   # 200 eV, pitch angle 150°
settings = TestParticleSettings.for_field(float(np.linalg.norm(b_local)), gyrations=500.0)
result = trace_test_particles(grid, r0, v0, b_external, settings=settings)
result.status                       # "surface_hit" / "returned" / "escaped" / "max_steps" ...
result.arrays["spacecraft_shell_pitch_deg"]   # pitch angle where the orbit returned to the start radius

for_field uses \(1/120\) of the gyro period as the time step and gyrations for the step budget. Reaching stop_altitude_km (default 6.1 km, the lower shell) gives surface_hit, exceeding escape_altitude_km gives escaped, and re-entering return_radius_km around the start gives returned. spacecraft_shell_* is the state at the first upward crossing of the start radius, the quantity to compare with a reflected electron seen at the spacecraft. There is no electric field, and outside the shell grid (bounds="nan") the status is invalid_field.

docs.title: Closed-field islands
docs.text:
from sopran.experimental.moon.closure import classify_closed_islands

islands = classify_closed_islands(
    lon_deg, lat_deg, closed_like, path_max_nT, footpoint_separation_deg,
    min_path_max_nT=10.0, min_footpoint_separation_deg=5.0, min_cells=3,
)
islands.island_id, islands.island_count

On a complete longitude × latitude grid, cells with closed_like true, path maximum and footpoint separation above the thresholds are connected with four neighbours and longitude wraparound; components smaller than min_cells are dropped. The physical meaning of the thresholds is the caller's.

docs.title: Field residual and quiet baseline
docs.text:
from sopran.experimental.kaguya.field_residual import (
    quiet_field_baseline, residual_decomposition, svm3d_residual,
)

residual = svm3d_residual(grid, position_me_km, observed_nT)   # observed − SVM3D
residual.parallel_nT, residual.perpendicular_abs_nT, residual.fractional_abs
baseline = quiet_field_baseline(lon_deg, lat_deg, b_sc_nT, quiet_mask, grid_deg=10.0, min_events=5)
compression = b_sc_nT / baseline.value          # B_sc / B_quiet

residual_decomposition(observed, base, direction) returns the residual vector, its component along direction (default: the observed direction), the perpendicular magnitude and \(|\text{residual}|/|\text{base}|\). quiet_field_baseline takes the median per grid_deg cell over the quiet_mask rows; cells with fewer than min_events use the global median, then fallback, and source records which one. In the lunarsat analysis quiet meant pressure and IMF below their medians outside the tail, and most of the ER field response to the solar wind was explained by \(B_\mathrm{sc}/B_\mathrm{quiet}\).

docs.title: Environment-response regression
docs.text:
from sopran.experimental.statistics.ridge import (
    external_gain, feature_drop_diagnostics, grouped_cv_predictions, model_ladder,
)

ladder = model_ladder(
    frame, targets=["log_b_eff"],
    specs=[("local", ["log_b_sc"]), ("physical", ["log_b_sc", "log_pressure", "imf_abs"])],
    alpha=1.0, folds=5, seed=0, group_column="track_id",
)
ladder.metrics          # train_r2 / cv_r2 / n_rows
drops = feature_drop_diagnostics(
    frame, target="log_b_eff",
    feature_groups={"local": ["log_b_sc"], "upstream": ["log_pressure", "imf_abs"]},
    alpha=1.0, group_column="track_id",
)
gain = external_gain(base_x, physical_x, log_target, alpha=1.0, eps=0.25)
gain.external_gain, gain.corrected

Features are standardized with the training rows and the intercept is not penalized. With group_column, rows sharing a value stay in one fold, so cv_r2 measures prediction across tracks. external_gain takes the difference of the log predictions of the base and physical models as the gain \(\exp(\Delta)\) and returns corrected = max(exp(y − Δ) − eps, 0). The regression metrics describe correlation, not causation.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Test particles are valid for a magnetic-only, uniform external field within the interpolation accuracy of the SVM3D shell grid; the altitude range of the grid (default 6.1–200 km) cannot be left.
  • The physical reading of a residual (external field, induced field, model error) does not follow from the decomposition.
  • Regression outputs are not written to the Store; save them together with the settings and input provenance.

docs.title: Spacecraft Potential Proxies And PACE Low-Level Tables
docs.text: sopran.experimental.kaguya.spacecraft_potential builds spacecraft-potential proxies \(V_\mathrm{sc}\) from steps in PACE energy spectra and matches them to event times. It does not solve a charging model. The values are correction candidates with a width, not measured potentials. In the May 2026 lunarsat trials the ESA steps were adopted, while the ion proxies kept a systematic offset of about \(-57\,\mathrm{V}\) against the ESA proxies and remained diagnostics. Precision is set by the ESA energy resolution and the thresholds; there is no independent full-period validation.

docs.title: Adoption rules
docs.text:
Proxy Condition Value Enabled by ESA falling step Day side (SZA < 80°) Spacecraft photoelectron boundary, \(V_\mathrm{sc}=+E_\mathrm{edge}\) use_dayside_photoelectron (default True) ESA rising step Night side (SZA ≥ 120°) Cold-electron cutoff by a negative spacecraft, \(V_\mathrm{sc}=-E_\mathrm{edge}\) always IMA/IEA low-energy ion peak Night side \(V_\mathrm{sc}=-E_\mathrm{peak}\) use_ion_proxies (default False, diagnostic)

The step is the adjacent pair with the largest difference of the 3-point-median-smoothed \(\log_{10}\) signal inside edge_min_eV–edge_max_eV (default 5–350 eV); cutoff_energy_eV is where the profile crosses the midpoint between its 20th and 80th percentiles. quality requires quality_score ≥ 1, built from the step height (≥ 0.25 dex), the profile range (≥ 0.35 dex), the number of bins and the low-energy count fraction.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import sopran as spn
from sopran.experimental.kaguya import spacecraft_potential as sp
from sopran.missions.kaguya.geometry import lmag_sza

kg = spn.Kaguya()
time = spn.day("2008-04-02")
esa1 = kg.esa1.load(time, calibration=kg.esa1.load_calibration())
times, energy, counts, eflux = sp.energy_spectra(esa1.to_xarray())   # look-summed spectra
features = sp.cutoff_features(energy, counts, eflux, settings=sp.CutoffSettings())
sza = lmag_sza(kg.lmag.load(time)).to_xarray().interp(time=times.astype("datetime64[s]")).values
cutoff = sp.cutoff_table(times, features, sensor="esa1", sza_deg=sza)
proxies = sp.proxy_table(cutoff)

events = ...  # polars.DataFrame with time_unix and sza_deg (for example ER windows)
estimate = sp.estimate_potential(events, proxies, settings=sp.PotentialEstimateSettings())
estimate.select("time_unix", "vsc_est_V", "vsc_sigma_V", "vsc_method")

estimate_potential picks the first available value in this order and records it in vsc_method:

  1. direct_proxy: a proxy of the same side (day/night) within direct_tolerance_seconds (default 60 s)
  2. time_smoothed_proxy: the rolling median of adopted proxies over smooth_window_seconds (default 1800 s), within gapfill_max_gap_seconds
  3. condition_prior: the median of the same side and SZA bin (sza_bin_deg, at least 3 rows)
  4. global_prior: global_prior_V (default 0 V) with global_sigma_V (default 60 V)

When the value enters an ER boundary model, the electron energy correction is \(E-U_\mathrm{sc}\). The sign passed as spacecraft_potential_eV (for example to FiniteBinObservation) is the physical spacecraft potential \(V_\mathrm{sc}\) of this table.

docs.title: PACE low-level tables
docs.text:
sopran.experimental.kaguya.pace_lowlevel turns decoded PBF1 records into tables close to the public files: the integer header fields (headers), per-record sums and maxima of cnt, event and trash with the number of fill cells (65535) (counts), and for IMA the 0x40 time-of-flight histogram summed over records and the four leading sectors as (energy_index, tof_index, counts) (tof).

from sopran.experimental.kaguya.pace_lowlevel import lowlevel_summary

tables = lowlevel_summary(kg.ima.load(time).pace)
tables["headers"], tables["counts"], tables["tof"]

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Steps are searched record by record; continuity between neighbouring records is not used. The quality thresholds are empirical values tuned for night-side cutoffs.
  • The day-side photoelectron boundary is not the lunar surface potential, which moves with solar activity and the ambient plasma (Kato et al.).
  • Do not adopt the ion proxies until they are validated against the expected solar-wind ion energy and coincident cold ions and electron beams.
  • Sources: Saito et al. (2010, 2013), Halekas et al. (2008), lunarsat working/kgy-er/notes/kgy-er-spacecraft-potential-strategy-2026-05-02.md.

docs.title: Wave Candidates
docs.text: This experiment extracts candidate intervals of wave events from KAGUYA LRS/WFC spectra. It covers the detection preset KAGUYA_WFC_V1, the quality mask, the validation intervals, and how to define the denominator of occurrence rates. Labels obtained here are automatic detection candidates, not confirmed physical phenomena.

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
import sopran as spn
from sopran.experimental.waves import detect_wave_candidates
from sopran.experimental.kaguya.waves import KAGUYA_WFC_V1, build_kaguya_wfc_quality_mask

time = spn.day("2008-01-10")
data = spn.Kaguya().lrs.load(time, kind="WFC")
spectrum = data.wfc_ey_power_spectral_density.to_xarray()
quality = build_kaguya_wfc_quality_mask(
    spectrum.values,
    mode=data.wfc_mode.to_xarray().values,
    gain=data.wfc_gain.to_xarray().values,
    fband=data.wfc_fband.to_xarray().values,
    postgap=data.wfc_postgap.to_xarray().values,
)
result = detect_wave_candidates(
    spectrum.time.values,
    spectrum.frequency.values,
    spectrum.values,
    input_scale="linear_power",
    config=KAGUYA_WFC_V1,
    valid_time=quality.valid_time,
    component="Ey",
    source_dataset="kaguya.lrs.wfc_ey_power_spectral_density",
)

window_features = result.features_to_polars()
events = result.events_to_polars(mission="kaguya", instrument="lrs_wfc_h")

confidence is currently an uncalibrated heuristic built from thresholds. Use the raw score for comparison and ranking, and do not read it as a probability.

docs.title: Preset KAGUYA_WFC_V1
docs.text:
The input is the WFC-H Ex/Ey power spectral density. Times are UTC and intervals are half-open [start, stop). Windows are 120 s long with a 60 s step. Features are computed in these bands:

Use Band (kHz) Intent low_broadband 0.1–10 Low-frequency broadband enhancement low_fpe 2–30 Low-frequency peak candidates (the 30 kHz line is not masked uniformly) ridge 10–100 Ridges, drift, frequency shifts radio 100–500 Broadband radio candidates high 500–1000 High-frequency diagnostics

docs.title: Fixed lines
docs.text:
Instrumental fixed-frequency lines are not removed from every band unconditionally. Each use treats them as follows.

Center Half width Use Treatment 30 kHz 2 kHz ridge, tracking Masked from ridge scores and tracking paths; not applied uniformly to single-peak decisions in low_fpe 200 kHz 12 kHz radio Masked from the broadband radio score; kept for separate radio-frequency interference (RFI) diagnostics 957 kHz 3 kHz high Masked from high-band derived features and cluster inputs; kept in raw summaries and RFI diagnostics 30/200/957 kHz 3 kHz each Clustering Excluded or turned into separate features so raw peak positions do not dominate clusters

The earlier tracker masked 30 kHz by ±2 kHz and raw-spectrum clustering uses a common ±3 kHz mask; the same FixedLine is not reused. 200 kHz and 957 kHz remain in detection, with physical candidate scores and fixed-line diagnostics kept separate. In particular, never use the 957 kHz maximum as the representative frequency of an event that occurred at low frequencies. The preset and feature definitions are stored in shards together with feature_spec_hash.

docs.title: Quality mask
docs.text:
build_kaguya_wfc_quality_mask returns per-value sample_valid, per-time record_valid, and warnings for state changes.

  • Spectral values that are NaN, inf, or CDF pad values (254, 65534) are invalid.
  • Times where Mode, Gain, Fband, or PostGap is NaN or a pad value are invalid.
  • Finite Mode, Gain, Fband, or PostGap values, or changes in them, never discard observations on their own; they only produce warnings, because stable non-default modes are scientifically usable.
  • Times where only some frequency bins are missing keep record_valid so the usable bins remain, and report the gap through sample_valid and finite_fraction. Times where every bin is missing are invalid.
  • Windows with warnings are not rejected automatically; the detector metadata keeps warning counts so people can review them.

Mode may be passed as raw values. When using decoded flags, evaluate xymode and omode as separate quality series and pass fband to its dedicated argument. No interpolation that changes the meaning of a state is applied.

docs.title: Validation intervals
docs.text:
tests/fixtures/kaguya_wfc_wave_gold.json is a small anchor set for catching detector regressions. It cannot serve as a complete event catalog.

  • strict_intervals have relatively clear quality and spectral shape, and candidates are expected to survive preset changes.
  • review_intervals are for people to recheck context such as state changes, data gaps, saturation, fixed lines, and solar radio bursts. Tests do not fail on detection alone there.
  • The "candidate type" given to intervals is not a scientific identification. When thresholds or background estimates change, review figures and features before updating.
  • Short spikes may be suppressed by the 120 s median. Misclassification into physical candidates by the main detector and the performance of short-duration detectors are evaluated separately.

docs.title: Rate denominators
docs.text:
The denominator of occurrence rates is the eligible exposure: the time the detector could actually decide, not calendar time or file counts. For each detector, component, band, and preset hash, accumulate only the time that has data, is record_valid, and has the required frequency bins.

With 120 s windows stepped by 60 s, summing window lengths double-counts overlaps. The basic implementation assigns one step of time to each valid window center, and stores as exposure_seconds either that non-overlapping time clipped at data boundaries or the union of valid time intervals. finite_sample_count depends on the sampling period and the number of frequency bins, so it is not used as exposure.

event_rate_per_hour = event_count / (exposure_seconds / 3600)

exposure_seconds == 0 means "not observed", not zero events or a zero rate. Daily shards store, besides event counts, the eligible, invalid, and warning seconds, the source product, component, detector name, and preset and feature hashes. To avoid double-counting events that span day boundaries, the final catalog deduplicates by event ID and half-open interval. The Store event catalog's rates() follows the same approach (Storing Data).

docs.title: WFC-H and WFC-L
docs.text:
WFC-H spectra support statements up to BBN/ESW candidate, broadband enhancement, ridges, and radio candidates. Confirming electrostatic solitary waves (ESW) requires checking bipolar pulses and the time waveform in WFC-L. Never mark ESW confirmed based only on WFC-H broadband spectra.

WFC-H and WFC-L have separate readers, source products, data availability, and quality conditions. WFC-H candidates can be saved without WFC-L, but their confirmation status stays unverified. Later matching uses a common event ID or overlapping UTC intervals, and times without WFC-L are not treated as negatives.

The public CDF sln-l-lrs-4-wfc-spectrum-v1.0 and SPEDAS kgy_lrs_load.pro cover WFC-H spectra. WFC-L is a 10 Hz–100 kHz waveform receiver, a different product from these public spectra and from the subsurface sounder sln-l-lrs-2-sndr-waveform-*. The current reader does not support WFC-L waveforms, and no guessed paths are registered as datasets.

docs.title: Shards and clustering
docs.text:
The first shard stores not only candidate intervals but also background differences, per-band statistics, ridge slopes and continuity, fixed-line diagnostics, quality warnings, and data availability and exposure. Clustering takes these reproducible feature shards as input and never calls mission-specific readers or raw CDF directly. Raw peaks at 30/200/957 kHz are excluded or separated into dedicated RFI features, and shards with different preset or feature hashes are never mixed silently.

Exploratory clusters come from fit_background_residual_clustering(result.windows.normalized_z). The returned integer IDs are local to each fit, so always store them with cluster_run_id. Clusters are never promoted automatically to phenomenon names or noise decisions; only interpreted labels are written to the event catalog as a separate detector version.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Y. Kasahara et al., "Plasma wave observation using waveform capture in the Lunar Radar Sounder on board the SELENE spacecraft," Earth, Planets and Space 60, 341–351 (2008). doi:10.1186/BF03352799. Used for the WFC-H/WFC-L instrument boundary and the 12-digit hexadecimal TI counter description on p. 350.
  • NASA/SPDF, CDF User's Guide. Used for the default pad values of CDF_UINT1 and CDF_UINT2.
  • DARTS KAGUYA archive. Used to confirm public product boundaries.

docs.title: Time Alignment
docs.text:
Instruments sample at different times. Stacking them in a figure works with each instrument's own times (Plotting), but comparing values or feeding statistics and machine learning requires aligning times explicitly. SOPRAN offers two ways.

Goal Method Attach another instrument's values to one instrument's sample times resample_like Build fixed-width time bins and a table of per-bin values from each instrument time_bins + SampleTable

docs.title: Match another instrument's times
docs.text:
esa1 = spn.kaguya.esa1.counts.load(time)
conn = spn.kaguya.lmag.magnetic_connection.load(time)

conn_on_esa1 = conn.resample_like(esa1, method="nearest", tolerance="2s")
altitude_on_esa1 = spn.kaguya.orbit.altitude.load(time).resample_like(
    esa1, method="linear", tolerance="10s",
)
method Value used nearest Sample closest to the target time previous Last sample at or before the target time next First sample at or after the target time linear Linear interpolation between the neighboring samples

Targets with no sample within tolerance become missing. For linear the condition applies to both neighbors, so it never interpolates across data gaps, and it never extrapolates beyond the source.

The function form spn.resample_like(source, target, ...) also accepts pandas, Polars (DataFrame, LazyFrame), and xarray objects in addition to SopranArray. Times are converted to UTC datetime64[ns] before matching. Duplicate source times raise an error. linear on DataFrames interpolates numeric columns only, and pandas DataFrames with duplicate column names are rejected.

docs.title: Build time bins
docs.text:
bins = spn.time_bins(time, cadence="10s", partial="drop")
bins.to_polars()     # index, start, stop, center, duration_seconds, is_partial

partial decides what happens when the range is not a multiple of cadence.

partial Behavior "error" (default) Raise an error "keep" Keep the short last bin "drop" Drop the short last bin

Bins of unequal width, such as per-event intervals, come from explicit edges with spn.time_bins(edges=[...]). Every bin is half-open, [start, stop).

docs.title: Build a table of per-bin values
docs.text:
features = (
    spn.SampleTable(bins)
    .add(sza, method="nearest", tolerance="5s")
    .add(wave_power, method="max")
    .add(density, method="median")
    .collect(join="inner")
)
method Value placed in the bin nearest Sample closest to the bin center (may lie outside the bin; limit with tolerance) center Sample inside the bin closest to its center mean, median, max Aggregate inside the bin first, last First or last sample inside the bin collect argument Effect join="outer" (default) Keep every bin; missing values stay missing join="inner" Keep only bins where every variable has a value fill=value Fill values left missing by outer quality_mask=array Drop bins where the quality flag is 0, False, or missing; applied before join and fill

When every variable uses the same method, write spn.align(sza, density, grid=bins, method="nearest", tolerance="5s"). time × component vectors expand into columns such as magnetic_field_x and magnetic_field_y. Time series and vectors are supported; spectra cannot be binned directly yet.

docs.title: Using the result
docs.text:
Call Returns features.to_polars() Table with time and one column per variable; layout="long" for a long table features.to_feature_frame() Variable columns only (include_time=True adds time) features.to_feature_matrix() FeatureMatrix with a numeric matrix, column names, times, and provenance features.metadata() Record of bins, per-variable methods, and join settings features.write_dataset(store, "analysis.wake_context", context=case) Save in the Store's features layer

FeatureMatrix.select("sza", "wave_power") selects columns; write_parquet and write_npz save it, and FeatureMatrix.read_parquet and read_npz load it back.

docs.title: Working With Arrays
docs.text: An endpoint's load() returns a SopranArray: an xarray.DataArray with the variable name, schema (dimensions, units, frame), time range, source files, and processing history attached. This page covers selecting, reducing, rebinning, converting to tables, and saving. Plotting is in Plotting, and matching another instrument's times is in Time Alignment.

docs.title: Inspect the contents
docs.text:
flux = spn.kaguya.esa1.energy_flux.load(time)

flux.info()       # name, dimensions, time range, units
flux.schema       # VariableSchema (dimensions, units, frame, aliases)
flux.trange       # loaded time range (TimeRange)
flux.files        # source files
flux.metadata     # type, name, time range, schema, sources, and processing history
flux.xr           # the underlying xarray.DataArray

metadata is JSON-ready and is used as provenance whenever figures or Store datasets are saved.

docs.title: Select and reduce
docs.text:
Common xarray operations are available on SopranArray directly. They return a SopranArray, and the schema's dimensions follow the result.

band = flux.isel(energy=slice(4, 12)).mean("energy")
positive = flux.where(flux.xr > 0)
hour = flux.sel(time=slice("2008-02-01T03:00", "2008-02-01T04:00"))

Use resample to average in time.

ten_min = flux.resample(time="10min").mean()     # mean, sum, median, max, first, last

For anything else, drop to xarray through flux.xr. The result is a plain DataArray without units or sources.

docs.title: Rebin
docs.text:
rebin re-aggregates any axis with numeric coordinates onto given bin edges. The same call works for energy, pitch angle, frequency, and map longitude or latitude.

coarse = flux.rebin(axis="energy", bins=[10, 30, 100, 300, 1000], reduction="mean")

# several axes at once with a mapping (pas is a pitch-angle spectrum)
pas.rebin(bins={
    "energy": [10, 100, 1000, 10000],
    "pitch_angle": [0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180],
})

reduction defaults to "sum". Counts add up; use "mean" for quantities such as flux that should be averaged. "median", "min", "max", and "count" are also available.

docs.title: Processing history
docs.text:
rebin, resample, peak_trace, resample_like, and transform append the operation and its arguments to metadata["operations"].

coarse.metadata["operations"]
# [{'operation': 'rebin', 'parameters': {'axis': 'energy', 'bins': [10.0, ...], 'reduction': 'mean'}}]

The history is carried into quicklook() records and into the Store manifest (parameters.operations) written by write_parquet(). sel, isel, mean, and where update the dimensions but do not add history entries.

docs.title: Convert to tables
docs.text:
Call Returns to_xarray() xarray.DataArray to_polars(layout=...) polars.DataFrame to_pandas(layout=...) pandas.DataFrame

layout sets the table shape.

layout Shape "auto" (default) "array" for three or more dimensions, otherwise "long" "array" One row per time; the remaining dimensions go into one pl.Array column "long" Fully expanded long table with one column per dimension coordinate

"long" has one row per element, so a full day of PACE time × energy × look becomes very large. By default more than ten million rows raise an error. Change the limit with max_rows, or lift it with allow_large=True. For instrument-level PACE results, esa1.to_polars("counts", reduce_look="sum") sums over look first.

docs.title: Save to Parquet
docs.text:
Save one array as a Store dataset with write_parquet.

record = coarse.write_parquet(store, dataset_id="analysis.esa1.coarse_flux", layer="features")
record.scan().collect()

A manifest, schema, and catalog are written with it, and store.scan_dataset(...) reads it back. Writing stops if the dataset exists; pass overwrite=True to replace or append=True to add. For long periods saved per day, Batch Pipelines fits better. Which Store layer to use is described in Storing Data.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The main things to configure are where data is stored (the Store) and the download policy. Settings come from the session, the user config file, environment variables, and the Project sopran.toml; explicit arguments always win.

docs.title: Choose a storage location first
docs.text:
With nothing configured, spn.kaguya, spn.Kaguya(), and spn.Store() all use sopran_data/ under the Project root. Without a sopran.toml, the Project root is the current directory, so each working directory would get its own Store. Set the storage location first with one of these:

Method Scope How Session setting The running Python process spn.config.use(store="/path/to/sopran_data") User config file Every process of that user spn.config.save_user(store="/path/to/sopran_data") Environment variable Processes that inherit it SOPRAN_DATA_ROOT=/path/to/sopran_data Project sopran.toml Inside that Project [store] data_root = "data"

docs.title: Session settings
docs.text:
import sopran as spn

spn.config.use(store="/path/to/sopran_data", download="never")

with spn.config.using(store="/path/to/other_data"):
    spn.kaguya.esa1.counts.load(time)     # another Store only inside this block

spn.config.reset()                        # clear the session settings

use and using accept store (or data_root and cache_root), project, artifact_root, download, frame, cache, and backends. They never modify config files.

spn.Store("/path") only creates a Store object; it does not change the Store used by spn.kaguya. Use spn.config.use(store=...) to change it for the short entry points.

docs.title: User config file
docs.text:
spn.config.save_user(...) saves the same arguments to the user config file. You can also edit the file directly.

OS Location Windows %APPDATA%\sopran\config.toml macOS ~/Library/Application Support/sopran/config.toml Linux $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/sopran/config.toml (or ~/.config/sopran/config.toml)

SOPRAN_CONFIG selects a specific file. If the file above does not exist and the legacy ~/.sopran/config.toml does, the legacy file is read. Relative paths resolve against the config file's directory.

[store]
data_root = "/path/to/sopran_data"
cache_root = "/path/to/sopran_cache"   # defaults to <data_root>/cache

[defaults]
download = "missing"
frame = "SSE"
cache = true

[backends]
frames = "spiceypy"
plot = "matplotlib"

[project]
root = "/path/to/default_project"       # default Project for the short entry points
artifact_root = "artifacts"

docs.title: Project sopran.toml
docs.text:
spn.view(...) and the short entry points such as spn.kaguya use the first sopran.toml found from the current directory upward as the Project settings. Relative paths resolve against the Project directory.

[project]
artifact_root = "artifacts"

[store]
data_root = "data"
cache_root = "cache"

[defaults]
frame = "SSE"
download = "never"

[defaults.region]
body = "moon"
lon = [350, 10]
lat = [-5, 5]
lon_domain = "0_360"

[backends]
frames = "spiceypy"

[cases.example]
start = "2008-02-01T00:00:00"
stop = "2008-02-02T00:00:00"

The [cases.*] format is described in Time, Regions, And Cases.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Role SOPRAN_CONFIG Path of the user config file SOPRAN_DATA_ROOT Store root SOPRAN_CACHE_ROOT Cache root; defaults to <Store root>/cache SOPRAN_ARTIFACT_ROOT Where project.save() writes SOPRAN_DOWNLOAD_MODE Default download policy SOPRAN_OFFLINE When 1, true, yes, or on, the default download policy becomes never

docs.title: Download policy
docs.text:
Value Behavior missing (default) Retrieve only source files missing from the Store never No network access. Missing files raise or give empty results, depending on missing= always Retrieve again even when files exist

Set it on mission objects (spn.Kaguya(download=...)), on a View, or per call (load(download=...)). On machines without outbound network access, such as supercomputer compute nodes, set SOPRAN_OFFLINE=1. Environment variables outrank config files (sopran.toml, user config), so the machine stays offline even when a file says download = "missing". Values set in code (arguments, spn.config.use) outrank environment variables.

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text:
Earlier entries win.

Setting Precedence Store root argument (Store(root), store=) > session > SOPRAN_DATA_ROOT > Project [store] > user [store] > <Project root>/sopran_data Cache root cache_root and SOPRAN_CACHE_ROOT in the same order as above, otherwise <Store root>/cache Project root (short entry points, spn.view, spn.Store()) session project= > first sopran.toml found upward > user [project].root > current directory Artifact root argument > session > SOPRAN_ARTIFACT_ROOT > Project [project] > user [project] > Project root Download argument (load, mission, View) > session > SOPRAN_OFFLINE > SOPRAN_DOWNLOAD_MODE > Case value > Project [defaults] > user [defaults] > missing frame, cache argument > session > Project [defaults] > user [defaults] Backends argument > session > Project [backends] > user [backends] > automatic Case region [cases.<name>.region] > [defaults.region]

The Store root and the download policy resolve in the same order whether you use a short entry point such as spn.kaguya, an explicit object such as spn.Kaguya(), spn.Store(), or a View or Case.

You normally do not set backends. Coordinate transforms choose one from the source and target frames (Coordinate Frames).

Invalid values, such as an unknown download policy or a key that should be a table, raise ConfigError.

docs.title: Coordinate Frames
docs.text: Vector quantities (magnetic field, position) carry their frame in the schema. For example, LMAG magnetic_field is in MOON_ME and magnetic_field_gse in GSE. Transforms to other frames are explicit with transform(), and the conditions used, such as SPICE kernels, are collected in a FrameContext and kept as provenance.

docs.title: Transform
docs.text:
# pass kernels (here a meta-kernel) that define both the source and target frames
frames = spn.FrameContext(spice_kernels=("kernels/kaguya.tm",))

b = spn.kaguya.lmag.magnetic_field.load(time)        # MOON_ME
b_sc = b.transform("SELENE_M_SPACECRAFT", context=frames)
b_sc.metadata["operations"]                           # record of source, target, backend, and kernels

Arrays of three-component vectors with times can be transformed directly.

frames.transform_vectors(
    [[1.0, 0.0, 0.0]],
    times=["2008-01-01T00:00:00"],
    source_frame="MOON_ME",
    target_frame="SELENE_M_SPACECRAFT",
)

From a View, view.frame_context() uses the SPICE kernels, time scale, and backend set on the view.

docs.title: Transform rules
docs.text:
• A transform to the same frame is recorded as an identity transform.
  • Transforms between different frames currently use spiceypy (SPICE). Pass a leap-second kernel and the frame kernels and ephemerides that define both frames in spice_kernels. If something is missing, SOPRAN stops with FrameTransformError instead of guessing. SSE and GSE are not in NAIF's generic kernels, so they need a frame kernel that defines them.
  • Transforms among GSE, GSM, and SM are planned to use spacepy and are not implemented. frames.plan("GSE", "GSM") reports status "planned", and attempting the transform raises FrameTransformError.

frames.plan(source, target) returns the selected backend and status (applied, implemented, planned) without running anything. frames.metadata() separates the backends installed in the environment (available_backends) from those SOPRAN treats as implemented (implemented_backends).

You normally do not choose a backend. Fix one only when the research requires it, with FrameContext(default_backend="spiceypy") or project.view(..., backend={"frames": "spiceypy"}).

docs.title: Getting SPICE kernels
docs.text: When KAGUYA orbit.sza gets no kernels and the download policy is not never, it fetches NAIF generic kernels (leap seconds, lunar frames, DE421) into the Store's raw/spice/kernels/. For other transforms, prepare the kernels and pass them to FrameContext. Kernels including KAGUYA attitude are available from sopran.missions.kaguya.selene_spice_kernels(store, time).

docs.title: Common frames
docs.text: Name Meaning MOON_ME Moon-fixed Mean Earth/Polar Axis frame SSE Moon-centered Selenocentric Solar Ecliptic frame GSE Earth-centered Geocentric Solar Ecliptic frame GSM Earth-centered Geocentric Solar Magnetospheric frame SELENE_M_SPACECRAFT KAGUYA (SELENE) spacecraft frame; the reference for PACE viewing directions

docs.title: Batch Pipelines
docs.text:
Use Pipeline to retrieve and decode days to months of data and save it to the Store as daily Parquet shards. For a single day in a notebook, load() and write_parquet() are enough (Working With Arrays).

Supported sources

Only KAGUYA PACE (esa1, esa2, ima, iea) currently has a Pipeline execution backend. Calling run(), scan(), or stream() on endpoints without one, such as LRS, raises PipelineError.

docs.title: Arrange stages
docs.text:
A Pipeline is created from an endpoint's pipeline(time); add stages and execute with run() at the end. Adding stages runs nothing.

time = spn.period("2008-01-01", "2008-01-04")

pipe = (
    spn.kaguya.esa1.energy_flux.pipeline(time)
    .calibrate(calibration="auto")
    .quicklook("esa1_energy_flux")
    .write("kaguya.esa1.energy_flux", layer="normalized", partition="day")
)
Stage Meaning download(), decode(), normalize() Make source retrieval, decoding, and normalization explicit calibrate(...) Apply calibration (PACE energy_flux) select_variables(...) Choose several variables of an instrument (when built from the instrument's pipeline()) quicklook(name, ...) After saving, write PNG and JSON to the dataset's preview/ write(dataset_id, layer=..., partition="day") Set the output; partition="day" writes daily shards from_normalized() Read a dataset already saved in the Store instead of source files

docs.title: Check before running
docs.text:
pipe.plan()                    # inputs, stages, output
result = pipe.run(dry_run=True)
print(result)                  # same result format, nothing executed

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
result = pipe.run()
result.to_dict()               # status, run ID, output dataset, log path

To protect existing datasets, a run stops by default if the output already exists.

Argument Behavior mode="create" (default) Stop if the output exists mode="append" Add shards mode="replace" Replace; not supported with PACE daily shards resume=True Reuse completed ranges; do nothing if the whole range is complete only_failed=True Rebuild only failed shards on_error="continue" Continue after a shard fails and record it as failed (default "fail" stops) download="never" Change the download policy for this run only

Every run gets a run ID, and the dataset's logs/<run_id>.json records start and end times, row counts, and shard counts per stage. The manifest's provenance also holds the stage list, time range, download policy, and run ID.

docs.title: Read saved data
docs.text:
lazy = spn.kaguya.esa1.counts.pipeline(time).from_normalized().scan()      # Polars LazyFrame
frame = spn.kaguya.esa1.counts.pipeline(time).from_normalized().collect()

for day_frame in pipe.stream(partition="day"):
    process(day_frame)

stream supports "all" and "day", and for PACE also "shard" for each saved shard.

docs.title: Heavy full-period computations
docs.text: Heavy processing over the full mission, such as model fits, uses separate CLIs designed around daily shards, resuming, and parallel runs. See ER Full-Period Batch for an example. Adding Pipeline support to a new data source is described in Adding A Data Source.

docs.title: Plotting
docs.text: SOPRAN figures come in two forms: plot() for a quick look at one array, and PlotStack for several instruments stacked on a shared time axis. Both use Matplotlib and label axes and colorbars with variable names and units. Plotting needs the viz extra.

docs.title: Look at one array
docs.text:
flux = spn.kaguya.esa1.energy_flux.load(time)
result = flux.plot()

plot() picks the figure type from the dimensions (mode="auto").

Dimensions Default figure time only Line time × energy × pitch_angle Two panels: pitch angle vs time and energy vs time Any other two or more (time × energy, time × energy × look, …) Spectrogram: time on x, a coordinate such as energy on y, value as color. Extra dimensions are reduced with reduction (default "sum")

Pass mode="line", "spectrogram", "pitch", or "energy" to fix the type. Use mode="raw" for xarray's own plot(). Plot vectors such as the magnetic field as component lines with lines(components="xyz"), described below.

Adjust the visible range and scales with:

Argument Example y range and scale ylim=(10, 10000), yscale="log" color range and log color vmin=1e6, vmax=1e9, log_color=True coordinate on y y="energy"

Quantities spanning many decades, such as energy flux, use logarithmic color and energy axes by default, as set in the schema (log_scale, log_dims). PACE energy_flux and ARTEMIS ion_energy_flux and electron_energy_flux carry these hints today. Pass yscale="linear" and log_color=False for linear scales. The defaults are the same for array plot(), quicklook(), and spectrogram() and for the endpoint call spn.kaguya.esa1.energy_flux.plot(time).

docs.title: Stack several instruments
docs.text:
Build multi-panel figures sharing the time axis with spn.stack(). This corresponds to SPEDAS tplot.

stack = spn.stack(
    spn.kaguya.esa1.counts.load(time).spectrogram(y="energy", log_color=True),
    spn.kaguya.lmag.magnetic_field.load(time).lines(components="xyz"),
    spn.kaguya.orbit.altitude.load(time, cache="use").line(),
)
result = stack.plot()

Array methods create the panels.

Method Panel spectrogram(y=...) Spectrogram; also takes log_color, ylim, vmin, vmax line() One-dimensional time series lines(components="xyz") Vector components; components="xz" selects a subset histogram(bins=50) Value distribution pitch_spectrogram(), energy_spectrogram(pitch=(0, 30)) Cuts through a pitch-angle spectrum

Each panel keeps its instrument's own sample times; nothing is interpolated in time. To compare values at common times, use the methods in Time Alignment.

Endpoints also provide spectrogram() and friends. Those panels load data when stack.plot() runs.

view = spn.view(time=time)
stack = spn.stack(
    view.kaguya.esa1.energy_flux.spectrogram(y="energy"),
    view.kaguya.lmag.magnetic_field.lines(components="xyz"),
)
stack.plan()     # check what will be loaded before running

Results from plot() can also be passed to spn.stack(), so figures tried one by one in a notebook can be combined later.

docs.title: Overlay spectral peaks
docs.text:
peak_trace(axis="energy") returns, for each time, the energy where the value peaks. overlay() draws it on top of a spectrogram.

ima = spn.kaguya.ima.counts.load(time)
peak = ima.peak_trace(axis="energy", min_value=5.0)

spn.stack(
    ima.spectrogram(y="energy", log_color=True).overlay(peak.line(name="energy_peak")),
).plot()

Use max_peaks=2 for several peaks and method="prominence" to select by prominence. Extra dimensions such as look are summed first by default. This is a candidate extraction for visual inspection; define and verify your own criteria before using peaks in an analysis.

docs.title: Fine-tune with Matplotlib
docs.text:
The PlotResult from plot() exposes Matplotlib's fig and axes.

result = stack.plot()
result.axes[0].set_ylim(10, 1000)
result.fig.suptitle("IMA / LMAG")

To apply the same changes before saving, pass a function as configure.

def configure(result):
    result.axes[-1].tick_params(axis="x", rotation=30)
    result.fig.tight_layout()

stack.quicklook("ima_lmag", root="reports", configure=configure)

docs.title: Save figures
docs.text:
quicklook(name, root=...) saves the figure together with how it was made. Both SopranArray and PlotStack provide it.

formats Files ("png",) (default) PNG and a JSON with the same name ("png", "html") Also a simple HTML page with the image and the record

The JSON records panel types, axes and color settings, time range, frame, and processing history. Passing context=view or context=case records those analysis conditions as well (Time, Regions, And Cases).

For interactive inspection in a browser, stack.explore() builds a Panel app.

docs.title: Moving A Store
docs.text: Sending inputs from a workstation to a supercomputer, or bringing results back, only takes copying Store files with rsync and rebuilding the indexes. This page gives the procedure and the rules that make it work.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
# on the source: list the files to send
sopran-store --data-root /path/to/sopran_data sync-list > files.txt

# transfer
rsync -av --delay-updates --files-from=files.txt /path/to/sopran_data/ host:/data/sopran_data/

# on the destination: rebuild indexes and check for missing or corrupt files
ssh host sopran-store --data-root /data/sopran_data rebuild
ssh host sopran-store --data-root /data/sopran_data verify

--delay-updates makes rsync put all transferred files in place at the end, so another job reading the Store during the transfer never sees half-written files.

docs.title: Choosing what to send
docs.text:
By default sync-list lists only datasets that SOPRAN creates and reuses by itself (managed=True): caches of orbit geometry, field-line connection, LRS, and pitch-angle spectra, and data availability summaries.

# select dataset IDs or ID prefixes (included even when not managed)
sopran-store --data-root /path/to/sopran_data sync-list \
  --dataset experimental.kaguya.er.paired_distributions > files.txt

# add part of the raw files
sopran-store --data-root /path/to/sopran_data sync-list --raw spice > files.txt

--layer and --variant narrow by layer and conditions. --all includes every dataset, including work in progress.

docs.title: Why it works
docs.text:
The Store keeps the following rules, so it works as the same datasets even under a different root path.

  • References are relative to the root. Manifests and catalogs never contain absolute paths. Files outside the Store are recorded only as a checksum and a hint of where they came from; they are never used for lookup.
  • Cache IDs come from content. variant_id is derived from settings and inputs (source file checksums, SPICE kernel names, hashes, and sizes). The same processing gets the same ID on every machine, so transferred results are reused as is.
  • Shard sidecars are the source of truth. Each shard is written to a temporary file and renamed, with <shard>.sopran.json next to it. catalog.parquet is an index that can be rebuilt from the sidecars. When other machines or jobs write different shards of the same dataset, a rebuild after the transfer merges them.
  • Machine-local files stay local. registry/, cache/, dataset work/ directories, *.sopran-tmp*, and *.sopran-bak* are never synchronized. registry/ is rebuilt automatically when manifests change. sopran-store excludes prints the patterns for rsync --exclude-from.

rebuild also creates sidecars for older datasets that lack them (migration).

docs.title: From Python
docs.text:
Command Python rebuild store.rebuild(), record.rebuild_catalog() verify record.verify_shards() Reference a file outside the Store store.file_reference(path)

Command options are listed in Command Line.

docs.title: Storing Data
docs.text:
A Store keeps retrieved source files, intermediate data created by SOPRAN, and analysis results you adopt under one root, separated into layers. It is separate from the Project workspace, so several Projects and machines can share one Store. Choosing its location is described in Configuration, and directories and file formats in Store Layout.

store = spn.Store("/path/to/sopran_data")

docs.title: What goes in each layer
docs.text:
Layer Contents Created by raw Source files from providers, with provider names and directory structure unchanged Downloads normalized Standard instrument quantities (counts, energy flux, magnetic field, …) as Parquet Pipeline, write_parquet features Quantities derived by SOPRAN (orbit geometry, pitch-angle spectra, data availability summaries, …) Caches, write_parquet models Calibration and model-fit results Experimental APIs, write_parquet databases Tables adopted per user or research topic (event lists, …) store.database, store.event_catalog cache Temporary files that can be regenerated Internal registry Search indexes Automatic

Each file in raw/ has a sidecar JSON (<filename>.sopran.json) with its source URL, checksum, and retrieval time.

docs.title: Caching avoids recomputation
docs.text:
Orbit geometry, field-line connection, LRS spectra, pitch-angle spectra, and similar products can be kept in the Store with cache=.

cache Behavior "use" (default) Read a result made with the same arguments if present; otherwise compute and save "refresh" Recompute and overwrite "never" Compute on the spot without saving

Results go under the dataset in the features layer (or similar), in variants/<variant_id>/ per set of conditions. variant_id is derived from the arguments and the content of the input files, so results made under different conditions never get mixed up. Results loaded with missing="empty" or "warn" while some source files were missing are incomplete and are not cached.

docs.title: Summarize data availability
docs.text:
Each endpoint's coverage() returns a daily or monthly table of observed sample counts and retrieved files.

daily = spn.kaguya.esa1.counts.coverage(spn.month("2008-02"), freq="day")

The columns are sample_count, finite_sample_count, sample_time_count, expected_remote_files, and available_source_files. The result is saved in the features layer as <dataset>.coverage and reused. It summarizes availability only; it is not an interpreted event list.

docs.title: Browse the Store
docs.text:
store.datasets(refresh=True)                       # every dataset (Polars)
store.datasets(layer="features", mission="kaguya")
store.raw_files(refresh=True, mission="kaguya")    # source files

lazy = store.scan_dataset("kaguya.esa1.counts", layer="normalized")   # Polars LazyFrame
frame = lazy.filter(...).collect()

store.dataset(dataset_id, layer=...) returns the dataset record (DatasetRecord).

Task Call Read completed shards record.scan() Inspect shard status record.shards(status="failed"), record.failed_shards() Verify shard checksums record.verify_checksums(), record.verify_shards() Verify including input source files store.verify_dataset(dataset_id, layer=...) Rebuild the catalog from sidecars record.rebuild_catalog(), store.rebuild()

docs.title: Research-topic databases
docs.text:
Group adopted results per topic in the databases layer.

db = store.database("lunar_wake", create=True)
db.register_product(name="event_table", schema=schema, description="hand-curated lunar wake events")
db.adopt_dataset(record, description="aligned context features")   # register an existing dataset without moving it
db.products()
db.product("event_table").scan()

adopt_dataset adds a dataset that lives in features (or another layer) to the database list without moving it.

docs.title: Event catalogs
docs.text:
Hand-picked events and detector output can be saved as validated tables with event_catalog.

catalog = store.event_catalog("lunar_wake", create=True)
catalog.write_events(events, time_coverage=spn.month("2008-02"), overwrite=True)

monthly = catalog.counts(freq="month", by=("instrument",))
rates = catalog.rates(exposure, freq="day", by=("phenomenon",))

events is a table with time_start, time_stop, mission, instrument, phenomenon, confidence, detector, and detector_version columns. rates divides counts by the time the detector could actually decide (exposure_seconds) and keeps periods with zero events as zero. To keep unobserved periods distinct from zero events, pass the decidable time aggregated separately as exposure.

docs.title: Moving to another machine
docs.text: The Store stays in a form that rsync can copy as plain files. See Moving A Store.

docs.title: Time, Regions, And Cases
docs.text: This page specifies time ranges and regions, the View that binds them, the Project workspace, and named Case conditions. For the workflow first, read Reproducible Analysis.

docs.title: Time ranges are half-open
docs.text:
A SOPRAN time range (TimeRange) includes its start and excludes its stop, so that concatenating daily shards never counts a boundary sample twice.

spn.period("2008-02-01T03:00", "2008-02-01T04:00")
spn.day("2008-02-01")      # 2008-02-01 00:00 up to 2008-02-02 00:00
spn.month("2008-02")
spn.year("2008")

ISO 8601 strings and datetime objects are accepted. Times without a time zone are UTC. A TimeRange has start and stop (UTC datetime) and the strings start_iso and stop_iso.

docs.title: Regions carry their longitude convention
docs.text:
region = spn.Region(lon=(350, 10), lat=(-5, 5), body="moon")

region.crosses_lon_boundary        # True (crosses 0/360)
region.contains(355, 0)            # True
region.to_lon_domain("-180_180")   # the same Region with longitudes in -180..180

Longitudes default to east-positive 0–360, latitudes to planetocentric. Change them with lon_domain, lon_direction, and lat_type. How Moon maps use these conventions is in Moon Maps.

docs.title: View
docs.text:
A View is an immutable bundle of period, region, and processing conditions.

view = spn.view(
    time=spn.day("2008-02-01"),
    region=spn.Region(lon=(120, 160), lat=(-45, -10), body="moon"),
    frame="SSE",
    download="never",
)
Kind Argument Effect Selection time (or start and stop) Default time range of endpoints Selection region Default region of Moon maps Selection mission, instrument, product, quality Recorded as analysis conditions Processing download Download policy of the missions Processing spice_kernels, time_scale, backend Used by the FrameContext from view.frame_context() Processing frame, cache Recorded as analysis conditions

view.kaguya, view.artemis, view.omni, and view.moon are real spn.Kaguya (and so on) objects. Methods use view.time when the time is omitted. Registered sources are also available as view.source("kaguya").

Create a new View to change conditions.

view.with_time("2008-02-01T03:00", "2008-02-01T04:00")
view.with_region(None)
view.with_context(frame="GSE", download="missing")

spn.view(...) uses the first sopran.toml found from the current directory upward as the Project settings. The short entry points such as spn.kaguya do the same.

docs.title: Project
docs.text:
A Project is the working directory of an analysis topic.

project = spn.Project("projects/lunar_wake")
project = spn.Project("projects/lunar_wake", store=spn.Store("/path/to/sopran_data"))
Item Meaning project.root Working directory that holds sopran.toml project.store Store in use; when omitted, resolved as in Configuration project.artifact_root Where project.save() writes project.view(...) A View with this Project's defaults project.kaguya etc. Mission objects without a time range

docs.title: Case
docs.text:
A Case is a named set of analysis conditions saved in sopran.toml.

[defaults]
frame = "SSE"

[defaults.region]           # default for Cases without a region
body = "moon"
lon = [120, 160]
lat = [-45, -10]

[cases.wake_20080201]
start = "2008-02-01T00:00:00"
stop = "2008-02-02T00:00:00"

[cases.wake_20080201.context]   # frame, cache, download, quality, time_scale
download = "never"

[cases.wake_20080201.region]
body = "moon"
lon = [130, 150]
lat = [-30, -20]

case = project.case("wake_20080201")
case.kaguya.esa1.counts.load()
case.with_time("2008-02-01T03:00", "2008-02-01T04:00")   # returns a View
case.view                                                # a View with the Case's conditions

Each key resolves from the Case value, then the session settings, then the Project's [defaults], then the user settings. download is the exception: session settings and environment variables (such as SOPRAN_OFFLINE) outrank the Case value (Configuration). project.case(name, start=..., stop=...) creates a Case on the spot without writing to sopran.toml.

project.save_case(name, view) appends the view's period, region, and processing conditions to sopran.toml and writes the same content to cases/<name>.json. It stops if the Case exists. Overwriting is not implemented, so edit sopran.toml to change a saved Case.

docs.title: Recording provenance
docs.text:
context= is the common argument that writes analysis conditions into figures, artifacts, and datasets.

Call Recorded in plot(..., context=case), quicklook(..., context=case) Figure JSON project.save(array, "interim/name", context=case) NetCDF and a JSON with the same name write_parquet(..., context=case), write_dataset(..., context=case) Store manifest

context accepts a Case, a View, an object with metadata() or to_metadata(), or a JSON-ready dict. A Case contributes its name, Project location, Store location, time range, region, and defaults.

project.save(value, name) writes anything with to_xarray() as NetCDF under artifact_root and records the time range, sources, and relative path in JSON. The Project holds temporary outputs; data reused across analyses belongs in the Store.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text: Reference for the main public classes and functions, generated from the source docstrings. For usage, see the User Guide and Data pages.

docs.title: Command Line
docs.text:
Installing SOPRAN provides the following commands. Each can also be called as python -m <module>.

Command Module Purpose sopran-store sopran.core.sync Synchronize, verify, and rebuild Store indexes sopran-env-check sopran.env_check Check the environment for building from source and the connection to remote data archives sopran-schema-docs sopran.schema_docs Generate the schema reference — sopran.experimental.kaguya.er_batch ER full-period batch (ER Full-Period Batch)

docs.title: sopran-store
docs.text:
sopran-store [--data-root DATA_ROOT] {sync-list,verify,rebuild,excludes} ...

Without --data-root, the Store from Configuration is used.

Subcommand Action Options sync-list Print files for rsync --files-from; by default only managed datasets --dataset ID (ID or prefix), --layer, --variant, --all (include unmanaged), --raw PREFIX (add a raw/ subpath) verify Check shards against catalogs and sidecars --dataset, --layer, --variant, --all rebuild Rebuild catalogs and indexes from sidecars; creates sidecars for older datasets --layer excludes Print patterns of files that are not synchronized (for rsync --exclude-from)

See Moving A Store for an example procedure.

docs.title: sopran-env-check
docs.text:
sopran-env-check [--native] [--sources] [--timeout SECONDS]

Checks the prerequisites for installing from source. --native checks the Rust toolchain for building the extension sopran._native and, on Windows, the MSVC build tools.

--sources asks each remote archive SOPRAN downloads from (JAXA DARTS, the Kyoto University PACE calibration tables, NASA NAIF, NASA SPDF, NASA PDS PPI, USGS) for one known file. URLs are built by the same functions the loaders use, and only headers are requested, so nothing is downloaded or written to the Store. Archives are checked in parallel, and server errors and timeouts are retried twice, 5 seconds apart. --timeout is the number of seconds to wait for each request (default 60).

Label Meaning Next step OK The file was reached. A redirect also shows the new location None MISSING The archive answered but the file is gone (404, 410) The archive has most likely moved or reorganized. Check the provider's site and fix the URL in SOPRAN UNAVAILABLE Server error (5xx, 429), timeout, or failed connection Usually temporary. Retry later; if it persists, check this machine's network ERROR Access was refused (403 and similar) Check access restrictions and proxies

The command exits non-zero unless every archive is OK. On machines that may not reach the internet, such as compute nodes, run it before starting a long retrieval. If there is no connection, set SOPRAN_OFFLINE=1 (Configuration).

docs.title: sopran-schema-docs
docs.text:
sopran-schema-docs [--check] [--language {ja,en}] [path]

Generates the Schemas page from the schema definitions in code. path defaults to docs/ja/reference/schemas.md. --check writes nothing and exits non-zero when the file is out of date (used in CI).

python -m sopran.schema_docs docs/ja/reference/schemas.md
python -m sopran.schema_docs --language en docs/en/reference/schemas.md

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Terms used throughout this documentation.

Term Meaning Endpoint The leaf object reached by walking mission, instrument, and quantity, such as spn.kaguya.esa1.energy_flux. Getting it reads no files; work starts with load() or plot() SopranArray The array returned by load(): an xarray DataArray with schema, time range, source files, and processing history attached Schema Definition of a variable's name, dimensions, units, data type, frame, and aliases (VariableSchema, InstrumentSchema). Written in code; documentation and validation are generated from it Alias A short name for the same variable, such as eflux for energy_flux or b for magnetic_field Time range (TimeRange) Half-open interval [start, stop); times without a time zone are UTC View Immutable analysis conditions bundling a time range, region, and processing settings Project Working directory per analysis topic that holds sopran.toml and outputs Case Analysis conditions saved by name in sopran.toml Store One root directory that keeps source files, intermediate data, and adopted results, separated into layers Layer A division of the Store: raw, normalized, features, models, databases, cache, registry Dataset One unit of data in the Store with a manifest, schema, catalog, and shards, named by an ID such as kaguya.esa1.counts Shard One Parquet file of a dataset; usually one per day Sidecar A *.sopran.json next to a source file or shard that records checksums and serves as the source of truth for catalogs Manifest A dataset's dataset.json, recording provenance, settings, and inputs Catalog catalog.parquet, an index of shard time ranges, row counts, checksums, and status variant A storage unit per set of conditions under one dataset ID; its ID is derived from settings and input content managed Marks datasets that SOPRAN creates and reuses by itself; the default target of synchronization Cache Keeping computed results in the Store for reuse, controlled by cache="use", "refresh", "never" Download policy How missing source files are retrieved: missing, never, always Provenance Record of the inputs, settings, and processing behind data or figures, kept in metadata, manifests, and figure JSON Processing history (operations) Record of operations such as rebin and transform and their arguments, in metadata["operations"] Quicklook A saved figure together with a JSON record of how it was made, created by quicklook() PlotStack A figure that stacks panels on a shared time axis; corresponds to SPEDAS tplot Native bins Time, energy, and viewing bins as recorded by the instrument, before calibration or rebinning look Index of a PACE detector viewing direction; not a direction itself, converted to one with the calibration tables Pitch angle Angle between particle velocity and the magnetic field (0–180°) FrameContext Bundle of SPICE kernels, time scale, and backend used for coordinate transforms SPICE kernel Data file for NASA NAIF SPICE with time, frame, ephemeris, or attitude information Rust extension The bundled native module sopran._native that handles heavy computation; users never call it directly Experimental API Research APIs in sopran.experimental, without compatibility guarantees Pipeline Mechanism that arranges retrieval, decoding, and saving stages to process long periods at once

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text: This page is generated from the SOPRAN schema definitions (InstrumentSchema). Do not edit it by hand: change the schema in code, then regenerate it with python -m sopran.schema_docs --language en docs/en/reference/schemas.md. The columns are the variable name, dimensions, units, data type, frame, aliases, and description.

docs.title: Store Layout
docs.text:
Directories and file formats of a Store. Usage is in Storing Data, and moving to another machine in Moving A Store.

/path/to/sopran_data/
  raw/          source files from providers
  normalized/   standard instrument quantities
  features/     quantities derived by SOPRAN
  models/       calibration and model-fit results
  databases/    tables adopted per research topic
  cache/        regenerable temporary files (machine-local)
  registry/     search indexes (machine-local, generated)

docs.title: Source files
docs.text:
raw/<mission>/<provider>/<provider path>/<filename>
raw/<mission>/<provider>/<provider path>/<filename>.sopran.json

The sidecar JSON records:

Key Contents path Path relative to the Store root filename, mission, provider, provider_path, version Identification at the provider download_url, acquired_at Source URL and retrieval time (UTC) checksum, size_bytes sha256 and size in bytes

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
<layer>/<dataset ID with "." replaced by "/">/
  dataset.json        manifest
  schema.json         variables, dimensions, units, frames
  catalog.parquet     shard index (rebuildable from sidecars)
  shards/             Parquet shards, each with <shard>.sopran.json
  logs/               Pipeline run records <run_id>.json
  preview/            Pipeline quicklooks
  work/               files of runs in progress (machine-local)

Daily shards use Hive-style paths such as shards/year=2008/month=01/day=01/part-000.parquet. Results under different conditions sit under the same dataset ID in variants/<variant_id>/, each with the layout above.

features/kaguya/lmag/magnetic_connection/variants/sphere_1737.4_both/

docs.title: Manifest (dataset.json)
Catalog (catalog.parquet)
docs.text:
Column Contents path Shard path start, stop Time range of the shard row_count Number of rows checksum sha256 of the shard status pending, running, complete, failed, skipped schema_version Schema version

Regular reads (record.scan()) read only complete shards.

docs.title: Sources of truth and indexes
docs.text: dataset.json, schema.json, and the sidecar of each shard are the sources of truth. catalog.parquet and registry/*.parquet are indexes rebuilt from them with sopran-store rebuild.

docs.title: Not synchronized
docs.text:
Machine-local files are never synchronized. sopran-store excludes prints the patterns.

*.sopran-tmp*
*.sopran-bak*
/registry/
/cache/
work/

docs.title: Exploring Data
docs.text: The previous page called spn.kaguya.esa1.energy_flux directly. This page shows how to find out, before reading any file, which variables exist and what loading them returns.

docs.title: Walking attributes does not read files
docs.text:
spn.kaguya, spn.kaguya.esa1, and spn.kaguya.esa1.energy_flux all describe where data lives. Getting an attribute never downloads, decodes, or computes anything. Work starts only when you call a method such as load(), plot(), or compute().

import sopran as spn

kg = spn.kaguya          # mission
kg.esa1                  # instrument
kg.esa1.energy_flux      # physical quantity (endpoint)

These docs call the leaf object that represents a variable an endpoint.

docs.title: Check before loading
docs.text:
info() prints a short description at every level. Endpoints also provide:

ep = spn.kaguya.esa1.energy_flux
time = spn.day("2008-02-01")

ep.info()       # description, dimensions, units, aliases
ep.schema()     # machine-readable dimensions, units, and frame
ep.plan(time)   # source files needed for loading
ep.guide()      # detailed instrument description (Markdown); English with guide(language="en")
ep.example()    # short example you can run

info() prints:

KAGUYA.ESA1.energy_flux
description: KAGUYA PACE ESA1 differential electron energy flux derived from counts with PACE INFO calibration tables.
dims: ('time', 'energy', 'look')
units: eV/(cm^2 s sr eV)
aliases: eflux, differential_energy_flux
example: kg.esa1.energy_flux.load(time)

dims are the array dimensions. PACE look is the index of a detector viewing direction, not the direction itself. aliases are other names for the same variable; kg.esa1.eflux reaches the same endpoint. The dimensions and units of every variable are listed in Schemas.

docs.title: What loading returns
docs.text:
An endpoint's load() returns one variable as a SopranArray. An instrument's load() returns an object that holds several variables measured at the same times.

flux = spn.kaguya.esa1.energy_flux.load(time)   # SopranArray
esa1 = spn.kaguya.esa1.load(time)               # instrument-level result

esa1.counts          # SopranArray
esa1.energy_flux     # SopranArray
esa1.to_xarray()     # xarray.Dataset with all variables

A SopranArray converts to other libraries' types.

You want Call xarray flux.to_xarray(), or flux.xr for the underlying DataArray Polars flux.to_polars() pandas flux.to_pandas()

Converting an array with three or more dimensions to Polars gives one row per time by default, with the remaining dimensions in an array-typed column. Use layout="long" for a fully expanded long table. See Working With Arrays for details.

docs.title: Back to source files and native bins
docs.text:
Calibrated or rebinned values alone are not always enough to check an analysis. SOPRAN results keep the source files and the records as decoded.

esa1.files           # paths of the source files
esa1.pace            # decoded headers and record arrays (None when no file was found)

To decode files directly, use sopran.missions.kaguya.read_pace_pbf(files).

docs.title: Loading by string ID
docs.text:
Scripts and batch jobs can pass the attribute path as a string.

counts = spn.load("kaguya.esa1.counts", time)   # same as spn.kaguya.esa1.counts.load(time)

The ID starts with a registered data source: kaguya, artemis, omni, or moon.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: When repeating the same period gets tedious, continue with Reproducible Analysis.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
SOPRAN is not on PyPI yet. Clone the repository and install it. Python 3.11 or later is required.

git clone https://github.com/Nkzono99/sopran.git
cd sopran
python -m pip install -e ".[full]"

[full] installs everything needed for KAGUYA, ARTEMIS, Moon maps, and plotting. If you know which data you need, pick only the extras from the table below.

docs.title: Building the Rust extension
docs.text:
A source install also builds the Rust extension sopran._native, which handles PACE decoding and pitch-angle binning. You need a Rust toolchain, and on Windows the MSVC build tools. Check them with sopran-env-check (it also works after installation).

.\.venv\Scripts\sopran-env-check.exe --native

On Windows, Chocolatey in an administrator PowerShell sets everything up:

choco install -y python314
