choco install -y rust visualstudio2022buildtools visualstudio2022-workload-vctools
refreshenv

python3.14 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install --upgrade pip
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e ".[full]"

docs.title: Choosing extras
docs.text:
pip install -e . installs only numpy and pandas; import sopran and the top-level entry points work, but nothing else. Each extra contains only the packages SOPRAN actually imports on that path.

Extra Use it for Packages kaguya Loading PACE, LMAG, and LRS; SPICE geometry cdflib, polars, pyarrow, scipy, spiceypy, xarray artemis Retrieving and reading ARTEMIS (THEMIS-B, C) CDF files cdflib, xarray moon GeoTIFF Moon maps, SPICE Sun direction rasterio, spiceypy viz Plots and interactive PlotStack views matplotlib, panel analysis, experimental Interpolation and experimental models scipy full All of the above

Loading OMNI needs xarray, and plotting it needs matplotlib; [kaguya,viz] covers both.

python -m pip install -e ".[kaguya,viz]"

docs.title: Checking the installation
docs.text:
import sopran as spn

spn.kaguya.info()     # list of KAGUYA instruments

If the list prints, you are ready. Decide where to store data and continue with First Plot. Development dependencies ([dev]) and how to run the tests are in Setup And Checks.

docs.title: First Plot
docs.text: This page walks through the electron energy flux measured by KAGUYA PACE ESA1 on 2008-02-29, from retrieval to plotting. It assumes network access and a Python environment with at least [kaguya,viz] from Installation.

docs.title: 1. Choose where data is stored
docs.text:
SOPRAN keeps retrieved source files and the intermediate data it creates in one directory called the Store. First set the default Store for the session.

import sopran as spn

spn.config.use(store="/path/to/sopran_data")

This setting lasts for the current Python process. Configuration shows how to make it permanent.

docs.title: 2. Create a time range
docs.text:
time = spn.day("2008-02-29")

spn.day returns 2008-02-29 00:00 up to, but not including, the next day 00:00 (a half-open interval). spn.period(start, stop), spn.month("2008-02"), and spn.year("2008") create ranges as well.

docs.title: 3. Plot
docs.text:
result = spn.kaguya.esa1.energy_flux.plot(time)
result.fig

SOPRAN then does the following in order:

  1. If that day's PACE ESA1 source file is not in the Store, download it from the JAXA DARTS public archive into raw/.
  2. Decode the file into a time × energy × look count array.
  3. Fetch the PACE calibration table (INFO) and convert counts to energy flux.
  4. Draw a spectrogram with time on x, energy on y, and flux as color.

The y axis and the colorbar are logarithmic by default, and the colorbar shows the variable name and units, such as energy_flux [eV/(cm^2 s sr eV)]. Set the visible range with ylim=(10, 10000), vmin=1e6, and vmax=1e9. From the second run on, the source file and calibration table are read from the Store without network access.

docs.title: 4. Load as an array
docs.text:
For analysis, load() returns the array.

flux = spn.kaguya.esa1.energy_flux.load(time)
flux.info()          # dimensions, units, and source files
flux.to_xarray()     # xarray.DataArray
flux.files           # source files that were read

The returned SopranArray is an xarray array with units, frame, provenance, and processing history attached. flux.plot() draws the same figure, and results of sel or mean keep the same type.

docs.title: 5. Save the figure
docs.text:
flux.quicklook("esa1_energy_flux_20080229", root="reports")

This writes a PNG to reports/ together with a JSON record of the time range, panel types, and axis and colorbar labels (with units). Pass formats=("png", "html") to also write an HTML page that combines the image and the record.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• To see which other variables exist and what you can check before loading, read Exploring Data.
  • To repeat analyses with a fixed period and region, read Reproducible Analysis.
  • PACE calibration and caveats are described in PACE.

docs.title: Reproducible Analysis
docs.text: Event studies compare several instruments over the same period and region, and record the conditions once they look right. SOPRAN uses View for temporary conditions, Case for named, saved conditions, and Project for the workspace that holds them.

docs.title: Bind period and region with a View
docs.text:
import sopran as spn

view = spn.view(
    time=spn.day("2008-02-01"),
    region=spn.Region(lon=(120, 160), lat=(-45, -10), body="moon"),
    frame="SSE",
)

view.kaguya.esa1.counts.load()            # the time defaults to the view's period
view.kaguya.lmag.magnetic_field.plot()
view.moon.sza.compute(subsolar_lon_lat=(0.0, 0.0))   # the region also comes from the view

view.kaguya is a real spn.Kaguya; only its defaults for time, region, download policy, and SPICE kernels are bound to view. frame="SSE" is recorded as an analysis condition. Coordinate transforms are explicit, with transform() from Coordinate Frames. To change only the period, derive a new View. The original view does not change.

zoom = view.with_time("2008-02-01T03:00:00", "2008-02-01T04:00:00")
zoom.kaguya.esa1.counts.plot()

docs.title: Create a workspace with Project
docs.text:
A Project is a directory per analysis topic. It holds the sopran.toml settings file, saved conditions, and outputs.

project = spn.Project("projects/lunar_wake")
view = project.view(time=spn.day("2008-02-01"), frame="SSE")

docs.title: Save a Case by name
docs.text:
project.save_case("wake_20080201", zoom)
case = project.case("wake_20080201")

case.kaguya.esa1.counts.load()   # loads with the saved period and region

The conditions are appended to projects/lunar_wake/sopran.toml, which you can also edit by hand.

[cases.wake_20080201]
start = "2008-02-01T03:00:00Z"
stop = "2008-02-01T04:00:00Z"

[cases.wake_20080201.context]
frame = "SSE"

[cases.wake_20080201.region]
body = "moon"
lon = [120.0, 160.0]
lat = [-45.0, -10.0]
lon_domain = "0_360"
lon_direction = "east_positive"
lat_type = "planetocentric"

docs.title: Save conditions with the figure
docs.text:
Passing context=case to quicklook() records the Case name, period, region, and Store location in the figure's JSON. Later you can tell which conditions produced a figure.

stack = spn.stack(
    case.kaguya.esa1.counts.spectrogram(y="energy", log_color=True),
    case.kaguya.lmag.magnetic_field.lines(components="xyz"),
)
stack.quicklook("wake_overview", root="reports", context=case)

Intermediate arrays can be kept as NetCDF with project.save(array, "interim/name", context=case). Data reused across analyses belongs in the Store, not in the Project.

docs.text:
